rules.rule_name: Initialize Output Files and Transaction Table
rules.rule_description: At program startup, the plain text statement output file and HTML statement output file are opened for writing, and the in-memory transaction table along with its counter are cleared to prepare for a fresh processing run.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
1:Initialize Output Files
Open STMT-FILE and HTML-FILE
Initialize transaction table and counters

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program has started execution and is ready to begin processing account statements
acceptance_criteria.When: The program initializes its output destinations and working storage
acceptance_criteria.Then: STMT-FILE and HTML-FILE are opened for output writing; the in-memory transaction table (WS-TRNX-TABLE) is initialized to empty; the transaction table counter (WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR) is reset to zero

rules.rule_name: Load All Transaction Records into In-Memory Table
rules.rule_description: Before any customer statement processing begins, all transaction records from the Transaction File are read sequentially and loaded into an in-memory table. This pre-loading ensures all transaction data is available for fast lookup during statement generation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
2:Load Transaction File into Memory Table
Read all records from TRNXFILE
Load into in-memory table by card number

acceptance_criteria.Given: TRNXFILE has been successfully opened and the first transaction record has been read; the card number of the first record is saved as the reference card number; CR-CNT is set to 1 and TR-CNT is set to 0
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads each transaction record sequentially from TRNXFILE
acceptance_criteria.Then: Each transaction's Card Number (TRNX-CARD-NUM), Transaction ID (TRNX-ID), and Transaction Rest data (TRNX-REST) are stored into the in-memory table at position [CR-CNT, TR-CNT]; reading continues until end-of-file is reached on TRNXFILE; upon end-of-file, the final transaction count for the last card group is saved and processing advances to open XREFFILE

rules.rule_name: Group Transactions by Card Number with Count Tracking
rules.rule_description: As transaction records are loaded into memory, they are grouped by card number. When a new card number is detected, the transaction count for the previous card group is saved and a new card group is started. This grouping enables efficient retrieval of all transactions belonging to a specific card during statement generation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
3:Group Transactions by Card Number
Detect card number changes
Maintain transaction counts per card

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from TRNXFILE and the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD) is available for comparison
acceptance_criteria.When: The current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) is compared to the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If TRNX-CARD-NUM equals WS-SAVE-CARD, the transaction belongs to the current card group and TR-CNT is incremented by 1; if TRNX-CARD-NUM differs from WS-SAVE-CARD, the current TR-CNT is saved as WS-TRCT(CR-CNT) for the previous card group, CR-CNT is incremented by 1 to start a new card group, and TR-CNT is reset to 1; in both cases, TRNX-CARD-NUM is stored as WS-CARD-NUM(CR-CNT), TRNX-ID is stored as WS-TRAN-NUM(CR-CNT, TR-CNT), TRNX-REST is stored as WS-TRAN-REST(CR-CNT, TR-CNT), and TRNX-CARD-NUM is saved to WS-SAVE-CARD

rules.rule_name: Open Cross-Reference File for Card-to-Customer Lookup
rules.rule_description: After all transaction data is loaded into memory, the Card Cross-Reference File is opened. This file links card numbers to customer IDs and account IDs and drives the main statement generation loop.

acceptance_criteria.Given: All transaction records have been successfully loaded into the in-memory table from TRNXFILE
acceptance_criteria.When: The program opens XREFFILE
acceptance_criteria.Then: XREFFILE is successfully opened and available for sequential reading; processing advances to open CUSTFILE next

rules.rule_name: Open Customer Master File
rules.rule_description: The Customer Master File is opened to enable keyed lookups of customer information including name, address, and FICO credit score during statement generation.

acceptance_criteria.When: The program opens ACCTFILE

rules.rule_name: Read Next Cross-Reference Record to Drive Statement Generation
rules.rule_description: The Cross-Reference File is read sequentially, one record at a time. Each record provides the card number, customer ID, and account ID needed to generate one complete account statement. The end-of-file condition on this file terminates the main processing loop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
7:Read Next Cross-Reference Record
Read next record from XREFFILE
Get card number, customer ID, account ID

acceptance_criteria.Given: The main processing loop is active and END-OF-FILE flag is set to 'N'
acceptance_criteria.When: The program reads the next record from XREFFILE by calling CBSTM03B with DD name 'XREFFILE' and operation M03B-READ
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the read is successful (return code '00'), the record data is moved to CARD-XREF-RECORD containing XREF-CARD-NUM, XREF-CUST-ID, and XREF-ACCT-ID, and processing continues to retrieve customer information; if end-of-file is reached (return code '10'), END-OF-FILE flag is set to 'Y' and the main loop terminates

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Customer Information by Customer ID
rules.rule_description: For each cross-reference record, the corresponding customer's full details are retrieved from the Customer Master File using the Customer ID as the lookup key. The retrieved data includes the customer's name components, address lines, and FICO credit score.

acceptance_criteria.When: The program performs a keyed read of CUSTFILE by calling CBSTM03B with DD name 'CUSTFILE', operation M03B-READ-K, and key value XREF-CUST-ID with key length equal to the length of XREF-CUST-ID
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the read is successful (return code '00'), the retrieved record is moved to CUSTOMER-RECORD, making available CUST-FIRST-NAME, CUST-MIDDLE-NAME, CUST-LAST-NAME, CUST-ADDR-LINE-1, CUST-ADDR-LINE-2, CUST-ADDR-LINE-3, CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD, CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD, CUST-ADDR-ZIP, and CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE for statement generation

rules.rule_name: Read First Transaction Record and Initialize Card Group and Transaction Counters
rules.rule_description: After the transaction file is opened, the first transaction record is read and used to initialize the card group tracking variables. rules.rule_name: Detect Whether Current Transaction Belongs to Same or New Card Group
rules.rule_description: For each transaction record processed during the loading loop, the system determines whether the transaction belongs to the current card group or starts a new card group by comparing the current transaction's card number against the previously saved card number.

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the transaction file and the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD) is available for comparison
acceptance_criteria.When: The system compares the current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) against the saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the card numbers are equal, the transaction is treated as belonging to the current card group and the transaction counter is incremented; if the card numbers differ, the transaction is treated as the first transaction of a new card group, triggering the card group transition logic

rules.rule_name: Increment Transaction Counter for Current Card Group When Same Card Number
rules.rule_description: When a transaction record has the same card number as the previously processed record, it belongs to the current card group. The transaction counter for the current card group is incremented by 1 to track how many transactions are associated with this card.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) matches the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD), indicating the transaction belongs to the current card group
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the card numbers are equal
acceptance_criteria.Then: The transaction counter (TR-CNT) is incremented by 1, reflecting that one additional transaction belongs to the current card group

rules.rule_name: Transition to New Card Group When Different Card Number Detected
rules.rule_description: When a transaction record has a different card number from the previously processed record, it signals the start of a new card group. The system finalizes the current card group by saving its transaction count, advances the card group counter to the next position, and resets the transaction counter to 1 for the new card group.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) does not match the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD), indicating a new card group is starting
acceptance_criteria.When: The system detects the card number change
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction count (TR-CNT) is saved into the transaction count array (WS-TRCT) at the current card group position (CR-CNT), preserving the count for the completed card group; the card group counter (CR-CNT) is incremented by 1 to move to the next card group slot; and the transaction counter (TR-CNT) is reset to 1 to count the first transaction of the new card group

rules.rule_name: Store Transaction Data in Two-Dimensional In-Memory Table
rules.rule_description: After the card group and transaction counters are updated, the current transaction's data is stored in the two-dimensional in-memory table. The card number is stored at the card group level, while the transaction ID and all remaining transaction details are stored at the specific card group and transaction position.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) is stored in the card number array (WS-CARD-NUM) at position CR-CNT; the transaction ID (TRNX-ID) is stored in the transaction number array (WS-TRAN-NUM) at position [CR-CNT, TR-CNT]; and all remaining transaction details (TRNX-REST, which includes transaction description, amount, and other fields) are stored in the transaction details array (WS-TRAN-REST) at position [CR-CNT, TR-CNT]

rules.rule_name: Update Saved Card Number After Storing Transaction
rules.rule_description: After storing the current transaction in the in-memory table, the saved card number reference is updated to the current transaction's card number. This ensures the next transaction can be correctly compared to determine whether it belongs to the same or a new card group.

rules.rule_name: Read Next Transaction Record from Transaction File
rules.rule_description: After storing the current transaction and updating the saved card number, the system reads the next sequential transaction record from the transaction file to continue the loading loop. The file access module is invoked with a READ operation and the result determines whether processing continues or the end-of-file condition is reached.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current transaction has been stored in the in-memory table and the saved card number has been updated

acceptance_criteria.Then: If a record is successfully retrieved, it is loaded into the transaction record area (TRNX-RECORD) and the loading loop continues by returning to the card number comparison step; if the end of the transaction file is reached, the system proceeds to finalize the last card group; if any other read failure occurs, the program terminates abnormally with an error message indicating the transaction file could not be read

rules.rule_name: Detect End of Transaction File to Finalize Loading
rules.rule_description: After each read attempt, the system evaluates the result to determine whether more transaction records are available or whether the end of the transaction file has been reached, which signals that the loading process is complete.

rules.rule_name: Save Final Transaction Count for Last Card Group at End of File
rules.rule_description: When the end of the transaction file is reached, the transaction count for the last card group has not yet been saved (since the save normally occurs when a new card number is detected). acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction counter value (TR-CNT) is saved into the transaction count array (WS-TRCT) at the current card group position (CR-CNT), ensuring the last card group's transaction count is correctly recorded; the in-memory transaction table is now fully populated with all card groups and their associated transactions, and the system proceeds to open the next required file (XREFFILE)

rules.rule_name: Open Customer Master File via File Access Service
rules.rule_description: The system must invoke the external file access service module (CBSTM03B) to physically open the customer master file (CUSTFILE), passing the prepared file control area containing the target file name and open operation request.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Request to Open CUSTFILE

acceptance_criteria.Given: CUSTFILE has been designated as the target file, the operation mode is set to OPEN, and the return status has been reset to zero
acceptance_criteria.When: The system calls the external file access service 'CBSTM03B' with the file control area (WS-M03B-AREA) containing the CUSTFILE open request
acceptance_criteria.Then: The external service attempts to open CUSTFILE and returns a completion status code in the file control area for the system to evaluate

rules.rule_name: Validate Successful Opening of Customer File
rules.rule_description: After requesting the customer file to be opened, the system must evaluate the return status from the file access service. A return status of '00' (successful open) or '04' (successful open with warning) are both treated as successful outcomes, allowing processing to continue.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: File Opened Successfully?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The external file access service 'CBSTM03B' has been called to open CUSTFILE and has returned a completion status code
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the return status code from the CUSTFILE open request
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the return status is '00' (open successful) or '04' (open successful with warning), the system considers CUSTFILE successfully opened and proceeds to the next step in the file opening sequence

rules.rule_name: Terminate Processing on Customer File Open Failure
rules.rule_description: If the customer master file cannot be opened for any reason other than a successful or warning status, the system must immediately display a descriptive error message identifying the failed file and stop all processing. This prevents any customer statement generation from proceeding without access to customer demographic data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Stop Processing
Program Terminated

acceptance_criteria.Given: The external file access service 'CBSTM03B' has been called to open CUSTFILE and has returned a completion status code
acceptance_criteria.When: The return status code is anything other than '00' or '04'
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE', display the actual return status code received, and immediately terminate the program abnormally — no further customer statements are produced

rules.rule_name: Customer File Ready — Proceed to Open Account File
rules.rule_description: Once CUSTFILE is confirmed as successfully opened, it becomes available for keyed lookups by Customer ID throughout the main processing loop. The system must then immediately proceed to the next mandatory step in the file opening sequence: opening the Account File (ACCTFILE). All four files must be open before customer statement generation can begin.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

Proceed to Open Account File

acceptance_criteria.Given: CUSTFILE has been successfully opened with a return status of '00' or '04' and is ready to serve customer demographic and address data lookups by Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the successful open of CUSTFILE
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must set the next target file to 'ACCTFILE' and transfer control to the file opening dispatcher (0000-START) to continue the mandatory file opening sequence with the Account File

acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the response from the file access service

rules.rule_name: Account File Ready for Statement Processing

acceptance_criteria.When: All four required files (Transaction File, Cross-Reference File, Customer File, and Account File) have been successfully opened
acceptance_criteria.Then: The system proceeds directly to the main statement processing loop, where it will read cross-reference records and retrieve account balance and FICO credit score information from the Account Master File using the account ID as the lookup key

rules.rule_name: Extract Cross-Reference Data from Successfully Read Record

acceptance_criteria.Then: The record data is mapped into the Cross-Reference Record structure (CARD-XREF-RECORD), making the Card Number, Customer ID, and Account ID available for downstream processing including customer data retrieval, account data retrieval, and statement creation

rules.rule_name: Set End-of-File Flag When Cross-Reference Records Are Exhausted
rules.rule_description: When the Cross-Reference File has no more records to deliver, the system sets an end-of-file indicator to signal that all customer-account-card relationships have been processed and statement generation should stop.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set End-of-File Flag, No More Records to Process

acceptance_criteria.Given: The file access service has been called to read the next record from the Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.When: The file access service returns an end-of-file condition (return code '10'), indicating there are no more Cross-Reference records available
acceptance_criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag (END-OF-FILE) is set to 'Y', which will cause the main processing loop to terminate and prevent any further customer, account, or transaction lookups and statement generation

rules.rule_name: Continue Main Processing Loop While Cross-Reference Records Exist
rules.rule_description: The Cross-Reference File drives the entire statement generation process. The main processing loop continues to read Cross-Reference records sequentially and generate statements only while the end-of-file flag has not been set, ensuring one complete statement cycle per Cross-Reference record.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Read Next Cross-Reference Record - Sequentially read the next record from the cross-reference file to obtain the card number, associated customer ID, and account ID for statement generation; set end-of-file flag when all records are processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The main processing loop is active and the End-of-File flag (END-OF-FILE) is currently set to 'N', indicating unprocessed Cross-Reference records remain
acceptance_criteria.When: The system evaluates the loop continuation condition at the start of each iteration
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the End-of-File flag is 'N', the system proceeds to read the next Cross-Reference record and, if the read is also successful (End-of-File remains 'N' after the read), continues to retrieve customer data, retrieve account data, create the statement, reset the transaction total to zero, and retrieve and write transactions; if the End-of-File flag is 'Y' at any check point, the loop terminates and no further statement processing occurs

rules.rule_name: Definitional Mapping of Cross-Reference Record Fields
rules.rule_description: The Cross-Reference record is the authoritative source that defines the relationship between a Card Number, a Customer ID, and an Account ID. Each record in the Cross-Reference File represents one unique card-to-customer-to-account association used to drive statement generation.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Extract Card Number, Customer ID, Account ID from Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully read from the Cross-Reference File
acceptance_criteria.When: The record data is mapped into the Cross-Reference Record structure (CARD-XREF-RECORD)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The following three data elements become available for the current statement cycle: the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) used to match transactions from the pre-loaded transaction table, the Customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) used as the key to retrieve the customer's personal and address information, and the Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) used as the key to retrieve the account's balance and financial details

rules.rule_description: The Customer ID used to retrieve customer information must always originate from the current Cross-Reference record being processed, ensuring each customer lookup is driven by the cross-reference data.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Take Customer ID from Cross-Reference Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully read and is available for processing, containing a Customer ID field (XREF-CUST-ID)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares to retrieve customer information from the Customer Master File
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Customer ID value from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CUST-ID) must be used as the exact lookup key, and the full length of the Customer ID must be computed and passed as the key length for the lookup

rules.rule_name: Key-Based Direct Lookup into Customer Master File via External Module

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Customer ID from the Cross-Reference record has been set as the lookup key and the Customer Master File (CUSTFILE) is open and accessible

acceptance_criteria.Then: The external module CBSTM03B must be called with the Customer Master File identifier, the keyed-read mode flag set, and the Customer ID and its computed length as the lookup key parameters

rules.rule_name: Successful Customer Record Retrieval Validation
rules.rule_description: After the Customer Master File lookup is performed, the system must validate whether the customer record was successfully found. Only a successful retrieval (return code '00') allows processing to continue; any other outcome must immediately abort all processing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Customer Record Found?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The external file access module CBSTM03B has been called to perform a keyed read on the Customer Master File using the Customer ID
acceptance_criteria.When: The module returns a response code indicating the outcome of the lookup
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the response code is '00' (success), processing continues normally; if the response code is anything other than '00' (record not found, file error, or any other condition), the system must display the message 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' and immediately abort all processing

rules.rule_name: Customer Record Storage for Statement Generation

acceptance_criteria.When: The system stores the retrieved customer data for use in statement generation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The entire customer record returned by the module must be moved into the CUSTOMER-RECORD working storage area, populating all customer fields including First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, Address Line 3, State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, and FICO Credit Score

rules.rule_name: Customer Full Name Construction for Statement

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved and stored, containing First Name (CUST-FIRST-NAME), Middle Name (CUST-MIDDLE-NAME), and Last Name (CUST-LAST-NAME) fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the customer name for statement generation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The full name must be constructed by concatenating First Name, a single space, Middle Name, a single space, and Last Name — each name component delimited by a space character — and stored in the statement name field (ST-NAME)

rules.rule_name: Customer Address Lines 1 and 2 Assignment for Statement
rules.rule_description: The first two lines of the customer's address must be directly copied from the customer record into the corresponding statement address fields for output in both the plain-text and HTML statement formats.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Retrieved Customer Record for Statement Generation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved and stored, containing Address Line 1 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-1) and Address Line 2 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-2)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares customer address information for statement generation
acceptance_criteria.Then: Address Line 1 from the customer record must be directly assigned to statement address field ST-ADD1, and Address Line 2 must be directly assigned to statement address field ST-ADD2, with no transformation applied

rules.rule_name: Customer Address Line 3 Construction with State, Country, and Zip Code
rules.rule_description: The third address line displayed on the customer statement must be constructed by concatenating the city (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, and Zip Code from the customer record, each separated by a single space.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Retrieved Customer Record for Statement Generation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved and stored, containing Address Line 3 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-3), State Code (CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD), Country Code (CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD), and Zip Code (CUST-ADDR-ZIP)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares the combined city-state-country-zip address line for statement generation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The combined address line must be constructed by concatenating Address Line 3, a single space, State Code, a single space, Country Code, a single space, and Zip Code — each component delimited by a space character — and stored in statement address field ST-ADD3

rules.rule_name: Customer FICO Credit Score Assignment for Statement
rules.rule_description: The customer's FICO credit score retrieved from the Customer Master File must be assigned to the statement output field so it is included in both the plain-text and HTML versions of the account statement.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Store Retrieved Customer Record for Statement Generation

acceptance_criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved and stored, containing the FICO Credit Score field (CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE)
acceptance_criteria.When: The system prepares customer financial information for statement generation
acceptance_criteria.Then: The FICO Credit Score value from the customer record (CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE) must be directly assigned to the statement FICO score field (ST-FICO-SCORE) for inclusion in the generated statement

rules.rule_name: Immediate Processing Abort on Customer Retrieval Failure

acceptance_criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' and immediately invoke the abnormal termination process, halting all further processing without generating any statement output for the current or subsequent customers

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Card Number from Cross-Reference Record for Transaction Matching
rules.rule_description: The program uses the card number stored in the current Cross-Reference (XREF) record as the key to search the in-memory transaction table. This card number determines which pre-loaded transactions belong to the current customer statement being generated.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Get current card number from Cross-Reference Record

acceptance_criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully read, containing a Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) that links the customer and account to their associated transactions
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins the transaction matching process for the current customer statement
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Card Number from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM) is used as the lookup key to search the in-memory transaction table for all matching transactions belonging to that card

rules.rule_name: Scan Termination Condition for In-Memory Transaction Table
rules.rule_description: The scan of the in-memory transaction table stops under two conditions: either all stored card entries have been examined, or the current stored card number is greater than the XREF card number. The second condition relies on the transaction table being in sorted order by card number, allowing early exit to avoid unnecessary scanning.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Scanned all stored cards OR current stored card number exceeds XREF card number?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The program is iterating through the in-memory transaction table using a card index (CR-JMP) starting from position 1, and the total number of stored card groups is tracked by CR-CNT
acceptance_criteria.When: The card index (CR-JMP) exceeds the total count of stored card groups (CR-CNT), OR the stored card number at the current index position (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is greater than the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The scan of the in-memory transaction table is immediately terminated and no further card entries are examined, ending the transaction matching process for the current customer statement

rules.rule_name: Card Number Match Verification Between XREF and In-Memory Table
rules.rule_description: For each card entry in the in-memory transaction table that has not yet caused a scan termination, the program checks whether the stored card number exactly matches the card number from the current Cross-Reference record. Only an exact match triggers transaction retrieval and writing.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does stored card number match XREF card number?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The scan of the in-memory transaction table is still active (termination conditions not yet met), and the current stored card number at index CR-JMP (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) has been retrieved
acceptance_criteria.When: The stored card number (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is compared against the card number from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the stored card number exactly equals the XREF card number, a match is confirmed and transaction processing proceeds for that card group; if they do not match, the current card entry is skipped and the scan advances to the next stored card entry

rules.rule_name: Set Active Card Number Upon Successful Match
rules.rule_description: When a card number match is confirmed between the in-memory table and the Cross-Reference record, the matched card number is formally set as the active card number for the current transaction processing cycle, establishing the context for all subsequent transaction writes.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Card match found - Set current card number for transaction processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: The stored card number at the current table index (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) has been confirmed to exactly match the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The card match is confirmed and transaction processing is about to begin for this card group
acceptance_criteria.Then: The matched card number (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is copied into the active transaction card number field (TRNX-CARD-NUM), establishing it as the card number for all transactions to be written in this processing cycle

rules.rule_name: Iterate Through All Transactions for a Matched Card
rules.rule_description: Once a card number match is found, the program iterates through every transaction stored in the in-memory table for that specific card group. The iteration continues until all transactions for that card have been processed, using the stored transaction count for that card as the upper boundary.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Start iterating through transactions for matched card - More transactions for this card?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card number match has been confirmed, the matched card group is at index CR-JMP in the in-memory table, and the total number of transactions stored for that card group is recorded as WS-TRCT at CR-JMP
acceptance_criteria.When: The program iterates through transactions using a transaction index (TR-JMP) starting from position 1 and incrementing by 1 for each transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The iteration continues processing each transaction as long as the transaction index (TR-JMP) does not exceed the stored transaction count for that card (WS-TRCT at CR-JMP); when the transaction index exceeds the count, iteration stops and the outer card scan resumes

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Transaction ID and Details from In-Memory Table
rules.rule_description: For each transaction within a matched card group, the Transaction ID and the full set of transaction details (including description, amount, date, and other attributes stored as TRNX-REST) are retrieved from the in-memory table using the combined card index and transaction index as the lookup position.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Retrieve Transaction ID and Transaction Details from in-memory table

acceptance_criteria.Given: The transaction iteration is active for a matched card group at card index CR-JMP, and the current transaction is at transaction index TR-JMP within that card group in the in-memory table
acceptance_criteria.When: The program retrieves the current transaction's data from the in-memory table
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID stored at position (CR-JMP, TR-JMP) in the in-memory table (WS-TRAN-NUM) is copied to the active Transaction ID field (TRNX-ID), AND the full transaction details stored at position (CR-JMP, TR-JMP) in the in-memory table (WS-TRAN-REST) are copied to the active transaction details field (TRNX-REST), making both available for statement writing

rules.rule_name: Write Transaction Line to Plain Text and HTML Statement Files
rules.rule_description: For each retrieved transaction, the program invokes the transaction writing routine (6000-WRITE-TRANS) which outputs the transaction details — Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount — simultaneously to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML-formatted statement file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 20: Write Transaction Line to Plain Text and HTML files

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction ID (TRNX-ID) and transaction details including Description (TRNX-DESC) and Amount (TRNX-AMT) have been retrieved from the in-memory table into the active transaction fields
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction writing routine (6000-WRITE-TRANS) is invoked for the current transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID is written to the plain-text statement file as field ST-TRANID and to the HTML file as an HTML paragraph element; the Transaction Description is written to the plain-text statement file as field ST-TRANDT and to the HTML file as an HTML paragraph element; the Transaction Amount is written to the plain-text statement file as field ST-TRANAMT and to the HTML file as an HTML paragraph element; all three fields appear together as one transaction line in both output files

rules.rule_name: Accumulate Transaction Amount to Running Statement Total
rules.rule_description: After each transaction line is written, the transaction's monetary amount is added to the running total for the current customer statement. This running total accumulates across all transactions for the current card and is ultimately written as the statement's total transaction amount.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: 21: Accumulate transaction amount to running statement total

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction line has been written to both output files, and the current transaction's amount is available in the active transaction amount field (TRNX-AMT), and a running statement total accumulator (WS-TOTAL-AMT) is maintained for the current customer statement
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction amount accumulation step is executed after writing the transaction line
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction's amount (TRNX-AMT) is added to the running statement total (WS-TOTAL-AMT), increasing the cumulative total by the exact amount of the current transaction; this updated total will continue to accumulate for all remaining transactions of the current card before being written as the final statement total

rules.rule_name: Skip Non-Matching Card Entry and Advance to Next Stored Card
rules.rule_description: When the stored card number at the current table index does not match the XREF card number, the current card entry is skipped entirely with no transaction processing, and the scan advances to the next card entry in the in-memory table. The scan termination conditions are then re-evaluated before examining the next entry.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: No match found for this card entry - Move to next stored card

acceptance_criteria.Given: The scan of the in-memory transaction table is active, and the stored card number at the current index position (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) has been compared against the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The stored card number does not equal the XREF card number (no match found)
acceptance_criteria.Then: No transactions are retrieved or written for the current card entry; the card index (CR-JMP) is incremented by 1 to advance to the next stored card entry; the scan termination conditions (all cards scanned OR stored card number exceeds XREF card number) are re-evaluated before any further processing

rules.rule_name: Initialize Card Table Scan from First Entry
rules.rule_description: When matching transactions to a customer's XREF card number, the scan of the in-memory transaction table always begins at the very first stored card entry, ensuring no transactions are missed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set Card Table Index to First Entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: The in-memory transaction table has been pre-loaded with card entries and their associated transactions, and a current XREF card number is available for matching
acceptance_criteria.When: The program begins the process of finding transactions for the current XREF card number
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card table scan index (CR-JMP) is initialized to 1, starting the search from the first stored card entry in the in-memory transaction table

rules.rule_name: Stop Card Table Scan When All Entries Exhausted
rules.rule_description: The scan of the in-memory transaction table stops when all stored card entries have been examined, preventing any out-of-bounds access to the table.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
All stored card entries scanned?
OR
Current stored card number exceeds XREF card number?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card table scan is in progress and the scan index (CR-JMP) is being incremented through the stored card entries
acceptance_criteria.When: The scan index (CR-JMP) exceeds the total count of stored card entries (CR-CNT), meaning every stored card entry has been visited
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card table scan terminates immediately and no further card entries are examined

rules.rule_name: Stop Card Table Scan When Stored Card Number Exceeds XREF Card Number
rules.rule_description: Because the in-memory transaction table is ordered by card number, the scan stops early as soon as the current stored card number is greater than the XREF card number being searched, since no match can exist beyond that point.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
All stored card entries scanned?
OR
Current stored card number exceeds XREF card number?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card table scan is in progress and the in-memory transaction table entries are ordered by card number
acceptance_criteria.When: The stored card number at the current scan position (WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP) is greater than the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) being matched
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card table scan terminates immediately, as no matching card number can exist at any subsequent position in the ordered table

rules.rule_name: Identify Matching Card Number in Transaction Table
rules.rule_description: During the card table scan, each stored card number is compared against the current XREF card number to determine whether transactions for that card should be included in the customer's statement.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Does stored card number match XREF card number?

acceptance_criteria.Given: The card table scan is active and the current scan position points to a stored card entry with card number WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP, and the XREF record provides the target card number XREF-CARD-NUM
acceptance_criteria.When: The stored card number (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is evaluated against the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.Then: If the stored card number exactly equals the XREF card number, the card is identified as a match and its transactions are eligible for statement inclusion; if the stored card number does not equal the XREF card number, the entry is skipped and the scan advances to the next stored card entry

rules.rule_name: Set Matched Card Number for Transaction Retrieval
rules.rule_description: When a stored card number matches the XREF card number, the matched card number is recorded as the active card number to be used during the retrieval and writing of all associated transactions.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Set matched card number for transaction retrieval

acceptance_criteria.Given: A stored card number (WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP) has been confirmed to exactly match the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
acceptance_criteria.When: The match is confirmed and transaction processing is about to begin for this card
acceptance_criteria.Then: The matched card number (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is copied into the transaction card number field (TRNX-CARD-NUM), establishing it as the active card number for all subsequent transaction retrieval and output operations for this statement

rules.rule_name: Process All Transactions for a Matched Card
rules.rule_description: Once a card number match is found, every transaction stored under that card in the in-memory table is retrieved and written to the customer statement, and each transaction amount is added to the running statement total.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Process All Transactions for Matched Card

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card entry in the in-memory transaction table has been matched to the XREF card number, and the matched card entry contains a count of transactions (WS-TRCT at CR-JMP) with each transaction storing a Transaction ID (WS-TRAN-NUM) and transaction details including description and amount (WS-TRAN-REST)
acceptance_criteria.When: The program iterates through all transactions for the matched card, from the first transaction up to and including the last transaction as defined by the stored transaction count (WS-TRCT at CR-JMP)
acceptance_criteria.Then: For each transaction: the Transaction ID (WS-TRAN-NUM at CR-JMP, TR-JMP) is set as the current transaction identifier (TRNX-ID), the transaction details (WS-TRAN-REST at CR-JMP, TR-JMP) including description and amount are set as the current transaction data (TRNX-REST), the transaction is written to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML statement file, and the transaction amount (TRNX-AMT) is added to the running statement total (WS-TOTAL-AMT)

rules.rule_name: Advance to Next Card Table Entry After Evaluation
rules.rule_description: After each stored card entry has been evaluated — whether it matched the XREF card number or not — the scan index advances by one to move to the next stored card entry, ensuring every card entry is considered until a stop condition is met.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move to Next Card Table Entry

acceptance_criteria.Given: The current stored card entry at scan index CR-JMP has been fully evaluated, either resulting in a match with transactions processed or a non-match that was skipped
acceptance_criteria.When: The evaluation of the current card entry is complete and the stop conditions (all entries scanned OR stored card number exceeds XREF card number) have not yet been met
acceptance_criteria.Then: The card table scan index (CR-JMP) is incremented by 1 to point to the next stored card entry, and the stop conditions are re-evaluated before examining the next entry

rules.rule_name: Set Current Card Number for Transaction Processing
rules.rule_description: When a card number match is found between the cross-reference file and the in-memory transaction table, the matched card number is set as the current card number to be used for all subsequent transaction processing for that statement.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Set Current Card Number
for Transaction Processing

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card number match has been found between the XREF card number and a card number stored in the in-memory transaction table at position CR-JMP
acceptance_criteria.When: The system confirms the card numbers are equal (XREF-CARD-NUM = WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The matched card number from the in-memory table (WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP) is assigned as the current transaction card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) to identify all transactions belonging to this card for the current statement

rules.rule_name: Iterate Through All Transactions for Matched Card
rules.rule_description: After a card number match is found, the system iterates through every transaction stored in the in-memory table for that card, processing each one individually until all transactions for the matched card have been processed.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
More Transactions
for this Card?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card number match has been confirmed and the current card group at index CR-JMP has a total transaction count stored as WS-TRCT at index CR-JMP
acceptance_criteria.When: The system iterates through transactions using a counter TR-JMP starting at 1 and incrementing by 1 for each transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The iteration continues processing each transaction as long as TR-JMP does not exceed the total transaction count (WS-TRCT at index CR-JMP); when TR-JMP exceeds WS-TRCT, all transactions for this card have been processed and the loop terminates

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Transaction ID from In-Memory Table
rules.rule_description: For each transaction belonging to the matched card, the unique Transaction ID is retrieved from the in-memory transaction table using the current card index and transaction index as lookup coordinates.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:
Retrieve Transaction ID
from In-Memory Table

acceptance_criteria.Given: The system is iterating through transactions for a matched card at card index CR-JMP and current transaction index TR-JMP within the in-memory transaction table
acceptance_criteria.When: The system accesses the in-memory transaction table at the two-dimensional position identified by card index CR-JMP and transaction index TR-JMP
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID stored at WS-TRAN-NUM (CR-JMP, TR-JMP) in the in-memory table is retrieved and set as the current Transaction ID (TRNX-ID) for use in statement output

rules.rule_name: Retrieve Transaction Details from In-Memory Table
rules.rule_description: For each transaction belonging to the matched card, the full transaction details (including transaction description, amount, date, and other attributes) are retrieved from the in-memory transaction table using the current card index and transaction index.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction ID has been retrieved for the current transaction at card index CR-JMP and transaction index TR-JMP in the in-memory transaction table
acceptance_criteria.When: The system accesses the remaining transaction data stored at WS-TRAN-REST at the two-dimensional position (CR-JMP, TR-JMP) in the in-memory table
acceptance_criteria.Then: The full transaction details (TRNX-REST — containing transaction description, amount, date, and all other transaction attributes) are retrieved and made available for statement writing, including TRNX-AMT, TRNX-DESC, and all other transaction fields

rules.rule_name: Write Transaction Line to Plain Text and HTML Statement
rules.rule_description: Each individual transaction is written simultaneously to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML statement file. The transaction line includes the Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount formatted appropriately for each output format.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: The Transaction ID (TRNX-ID), Transaction Description (TRNX-DESC), and Transaction Amount (TRNX-AMT) have been retrieved from the in-memory table for the current transaction
acceptance_criteria.When: The system writes the transaction details to both output files by invoking the transaction writing routine (6000-WRITE-TRANS)
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID is written to the plain-text statement line (ST-TRANID) and as an HTML paragraph in the HTML file; the Transaction Description is written to the plain-text statement (ST-TRANDT) and as an HTML paragraph; the Transaction Amount is written to the plain-text statement (ST-TRANAMT) and as an HTML paragraph — all formatted as a single transaction row in both output files

rules.rule_name: Accumulate Transaction Amount to Running Total
rules.rule_description: After each transaction is written to the statement, the transaction amount is added to a running total that will represent the total transaction amount for the current customer account statement.
rules.sub_graph_node_text:

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction has been successfully written to both the plain-text and HTML statement files, and the current transaction amount (TRNX-AMT) is available from the retrieved transaction details
acceptance_criteria.When: The system processes each transaction within the matched card's transaction list
acceptance_criteria.Then: The current transaction amount (TRNX-AMT) is added to the cumulative running total (WS-TOTAL-AMT), which accumulates the sum of all transaction amounts for the current card; this total is reset to zero at the start of each new customer statement cycle and will be written as the statement total after all transactions are processed

rules.rule_name: Write Transaction ID as HTML Paragraph Element in HTML Statement File

rules.rule_name: Determine If More Transactions Exist for Current Card
rules.rule_description: For each card number matched to the current XREF record, the program determines whether additional transactions remain to be processed by comparing the current transaction index against the total transaction count stored for that card group in the in-memory transaction table.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: More Transactions for This Card?

acceptance_criteria.Given: A card number from the cross-reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM) has been matched to a card group entry (WS-CARD-NUM) in the in-memory transaction table, and the total number of transactions for that card group is stored in WS-TRCT for the current card index (CR-JMP)
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction iterator (TR-JMP) is evaluated against the total transaction count (WS-TRCT) for the current card group
acceptance_criteria.Then: If TR-JMP is less than or equal to WS-TRCT, there are more transactions to process and the next transaction is retrieved from the in-memory table; if TR-JMP exceeds WS-TRCT, all transactions for this card have been processed and the loop exits to compute the statement total

rules.rule_name: Write Individual Transaction Detail Line to Statement and HTML Output
rules.rule_description: For each transaction belonging to the current card number, the transaction details — Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount — are written as a single line to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML-formatted statement file.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Transaction Line - Transaction ID, Description, Amount

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved from the in-memory transaction table for the current card number, with Transaction ID (TRNX-ID), Transaction Description (TRNX-DESC), and Transaction Amount (TRNX-AMT) populated from the stored transaction data (WS-TRAN-NUM and WS-TRAN-REST)
acceptance_criteria.When: The transaction detail writing step is executed for the current transaction
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction ID is moved to the statement transaction ID field (ST-TRANID), the Transaction Description is moved to the statement transaction description field (ST-TRANDT), the Transaction Amount is moved to the statement transaction amount field (ST-TRANAMT), and one transaction detail line (ST-LINE14) is written to the plain-text statement file (FD-STMTFILE-REC); additionally, the Transaction ID, Description, and Amount are each written as separate HTML paragraph elements to the HTML statement file (FD-HTMLFILE-REC)

rules.rule_name: Accumulate Running Total of Transaction Amounts for Current Account Statement
rules.rule_description: After each transaction detail line is written, the transaction amount is added to the running total for the current account statement. This running total accumulates the total expenditure across all transactions associated with the current card number and is reset to zero at the start of each new customer-account statement cycle.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Add Transaction Amount to Running Account Total - WS-TOTAL-AMT = WS-TOTAL-AMT + TRNX-AMT

acceptance_criteria.Given: A transaction detail line has been written for the current transaction, the Transaction Amount (TRNX-AMT) is available from the in-memory transaction table entry (WS-TRAN-REST), and the running account total (WS-TOTAL-AMT) has been initialized to zero at the start of the current customer-account statement cycle
acceptance_criteria.When: The accumulation step is executed after writing the transaction detail line
acceptance_criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount (TRNX-AMT) is added to the running account total (WS-TOTAL-AMT), resulting in WS-TOTAL-AMT reflecting the cumulative sum of all transaction amounts processed so far for the current card number on the current account statement

rules.rule_name: Transfer Accumulated Total to Statement Output Field for Display
rules.rule_description: Once all transactions for the current card number have been processed and their amounts accumulated, the final running total is transferred to the statement output field so it can be displayed as the total expenditure on both the plain-text and HTML statement outputs.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move Accumulated Total to Statement Total Field for Output Display

acceptance_criteria.Given: All transactions for the current card number have been processed, and the running account total (WS-TOTAL-AMT) contains the complete sum of all transaction amounts for the current account statement
acceptance_criteria.When: The total transfer step is executed after the transaction processing loop exits
acceptance_criteria.Then: The accumulated total (WS-TOTAL-AMT) is moved to the intermediate total field (WS-TRN-AMT), and WS-TRN-AMT is then moved to the statement total amount output field (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT), making the total expenditure available for writing to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML statement file as the statement summary total line

rules.rule_name: Transfer Running Total to Statement Total Amount Field
rules.rule_description: After all transactions for an account have been written, the accumulated running total transaction amount is transferred through an intermediate working storage field into the statement total amount field, making it ready for formatted output on the plain text statement.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Move Running Total Amount to Statement Total Amount Field

acceptance_criteria.Given: All transactions for the current account-card combination have been written to the statement, and the running total amount (WS-TOTAL-AMT) holds the sum of all transaction amounts processed for this account
acceptance_criteria.When: The statement total and footer writing process is triggered after the last transaction for the account is written
acceptance_criteria.Then: The running total amount (WS-TOTAL-AMT) must be moved to the intermediate total amount field (WS-TRN-AMT), and then WS-TRN-AMT must be moved to the statement total amount field (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT), so that the formatted total is available for writing to the plain text statement file

rules.rule_name: Write Separator Line to Plain Text Statement File
rules.rule_description: A visual separator line is written to the plain text statement file to delineate the transaction section from the total expenditure amount line, providing clear formatting and readability in the output statement.

acceptance_criteria.Given: The statement total amount field (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT) has been populated with the formatted total transaction amount for the current account
acceptance_criteria.When: The statement total and footer writing process writes the separator line
acceptance_criteria.Then: Statement separator line (ST-LINE12) must be written to the plain text statement file (FD-STMTFILE-REC) as the first output line in the statement footer section

rules.rule_name: Write Total Expenditure Amount Line to Plain Text Statement
rules.rule_description: The formatted total expenditure amount, representing the sum of all transaction amounts for the current account, is written to the plain text statement file as a labeled summary line, giving the customer a clear view of their total spending.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: Write Total Expenditure Amount Line to Plain Text Statement File

acceptance_criteria.Given: The separator line has been written to the plain text statement file, and the statement total amount field (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT) contains the formatted sum of all transaction amounts for the current account
acceptance_criteria.When: The total expenditure amount line is written to the plain text statement file
acceptance_criteria.Then: The total expenditure amount line (ST-LINE14A), which contains the formatted total transaction amount (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT), must be written to the plain text statement file (FD-STMTFILE-REC) immediately after the separator line

rules.rule_name: Reset Total Transaction Amount Before Processing Each Account Statement
rules.rule_description: Before retrieving and accumulating transaction amounts for a new account statement, the running total transaction amount accumulator must be reset to zero. This ensures that the total amount displayed on each account statement reflects only the transactions belonging to that specific account, and not carried-over amounts from previously processed accounts.

acceptance_criteria.Then: The total transaction amount accumulator (WS-TOTAL-AMT) must be set to zero before any transaction amounts are retrieved or added, ensuring the running total starts fresh for each account and does not include any transaction amounts from previously processed accounts

rules.rule_description: After all input files have been closed, both the plain text statement output file (STMT-FILE) and the HTML statement output file (HTML-FILE) must be closed together to finalize and flush all written statement content to permanent storage.

acceptance_criteria.Then: Both the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE) and the HTML statement file (HTML-FILE) are successfully closed, ensuring all generated statement content is permanently saved and available for downstream use

rules.rule_name: Enforce Sequential File Closure Order After All Records Processed
rules.rule_description: All six files used during statement generation must be closed in a strict, mandatory sequence after the main processing loop completes. The closure order ensures data integrity: input files are closed before output files, and the transaction file is closed first as it was opened and fully loaded first.
rules.sub_graph_node_text: All Cross-Reference Records Processed

acceptance_criteria.Given: The main processing loop has completed, meaning all cross-reference records have been read and all corresponding customer statements have been generated and written
acceptance_criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is reached on the Cross-Reference File and the program exits the main processing loop
acceptance_criteria.Then: Files are closed in the following mandatory sequence: (1) Transaction File (TRNXFILE), (2) Cross-Reference File (XREFFILE), (3) Customer Master File (CUSTFILE), (4) Account Master File (ACCTFILE), (5) Plain Text Statement File (STMT-FILE) and HTML Statement File (HTML-FILE) together — no file closure may be skipped or reordered, and the program terminates normally only after all six files are closed

key_functionalities.description: Close All Input and Output Files

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has started execution and is ready to begin processing account statements
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its output destinations and working storage
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: STMT-FILE and HTML-FILE are opened for output writing; the in-memory transaction table (WS-TRNX-TABLE) is initialized to empty; the transaction table counter (WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR) is reset to zero

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Output Files and Transaction Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: At program startup, the plain text statement output file and HTML statement output file are opened for writing, and the in-memory transaction table along with its counter are cleared to prepare for a fresh processing run.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: TRNXFILE has been successfully opened and the first transaction record has been read; the card number of the first record is saved as the reference card number; CR-CNT is set to 1 and TR-CNT is set to 0
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads each transaction record sequentially from TRNXFILE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Each transaction's Card Number (TRNX-CARD-NUM), Transaction ID (TRNX-ID), and Transaction Rest data (TRNX-REST) are stored into the in-memory table at position [CR-CNT, TR-CNT]; reading continues until end-of-file is reached on TRNXFILE; upon end-of-file, the final transaction count for the last card group is saved and processing advances to open XREFFILE

all_rules.Rule_Name: Load All Transaction Records into In-Memory Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any customer statement processing begins, all transaction records from the Transaction File are read sequentially and loaded into an in-memory table. This pre-loading ensures all transaction data is available for fast lookup during statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from TRNXFILE and the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD) is available for comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) is compared to the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If TRNX-CARD-NUM equals WS-SAVE-CARD, the transaction belongs to the current card group and TR-CNT is incremented by 1; if TRNX-CARD-NUM differs from WS-SAVE-CARD, the current TR-CNT is saved as WS-TRCT(CR-CNT) for the previous card group, CR-CNT is incremented by 1 to start a new card group, and TR-CNT is reset to 1; in both cases, TRNX-CARD-NUM is stored as WS-CARD-NUM(CR-CNT), TRNX-ID is stored as WS-TRAN-NUM(CR-CNT, TR-CNT), TRNX-REST is stored as WS-TRAN-REST(CR-CNT, TR-CNT), and TRNX-CARD-NUM is saved to WS-SAVE-CARD

all_rules.Rule_Name: Group Transactions by Card Number with Count Tracking
all_rules.Rule_Description: As transaction records are loaded into memory, they are grouped by card number. When a new card number is detected, the transaction count for the previous card group is saved and a new card group is started. This grouping enables efficient retrieval of all transactions belonging to a specific card during statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transaction records have been successfully loaded into the in-memory table from TRNXFILE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program opens XREFFILE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: XREFFILE is successfully opened and available for sequential reading; processing advances to open CUSTFILE next

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Cross-Reference File for Card-to-Customer Lookup
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all transaction data is loaded into memory, the Card Cross-Reference File is opened. This file links card numbers to customer IDs and account IDs and drives the main statement generation loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: XREFFILE has been successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program opens CUSTFILE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CUSTFILE is successfully opened and available for keyed record retrieval; processing advances to open ACCTFILE next

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Customer Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer Master File is opened to enable keyed lookups of customer information including name, address, and FICO credit score during statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: CUSTFILE has been successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program opens ACCTFILE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: ACCTFILE is successfully opened and available for keyed record retrieval; processing advances to the main statement generation loop

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Account Master File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Account Master File is opened to enable keyed lookups of account information including account ID and current balance during statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The main processing loop is active and END-OF-FILE flag is set to 'N'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program reads the next record from XREFFILE by calling CBSTM03B with DD name 'XREFFILE' and operation M03B-READ
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the read is successful (return code '00'), the record data is moved to CARD-XREF-RECORD containing XREF-CARD-NUM, XREF-CUST-ID, and XREF-ACCT-ID, and processing continues to retrieve customer information; if end-of-file is reached (return code '10'), END-OF-FILE flag is set to 'Y' and the main loop terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Cross-Reference Record to Drive Statement Generation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Cross-Reference File is read sequentially, one record at a time. Each record provides the card number, customer ID, and account ID needed to generate one complete account statement. The end-of-file condition on this file terminates the main processing loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A cross-reference record has been successfully read and XREF-CUST-ID is available as the customer lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs a keyed read of CUSTFILE by calling CBSTM03B with DD name 'CUSTFILE', operation M03B-READ-K, and key value XREF-CUST-ID with key length equal to the length of XREF-CUST-ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the read is successful (return code '00'), the retrieved record is moved to CUSTOMER-RECORD, making available CUST-FIRST-NAME, CUST-MIDDLE-NAME, CUST-LAST-NAME, CUST-ADDR-LINE-1, CUST-ADDR-LINE-2, CUST-ADDR-LINE-3, CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD, CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD, CUST-ADDR-ZIP, and CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE for statement generation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Customer Information by Customer ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each cross-reference record, the corresponding customer's full details are retrieved from the Customer Master File using the Customer ID as the lookup key. The retrieved data includes the customer's name components, address lines, and FICO credit score.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A cross-reference record has been successfully read and XREF-ACCT-ID is available as the account lookup key
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program performs a keyed read of ACCTFILE by calling CBSTM03B with DD name 'ACCTFILE', operation M03B-READ-K, and key value XREF-ACCT-ID with key length equal to the length of XREF-ACCT-ID
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the read is successful (return code '00'), the retrieved record is moved to ACCOUNT-RECORD, making available ACCT-ID and ACCT-CURR-BAL for inclusion in the account statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Account Information by Account ID
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each cross-reference record, the corresponding account details are retrieved from the Account Master File using the Account ID as the lookup key. The retrieved data includes the account ID and current balance.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Customer record has been retrieved and CUST-FIRST-NAME, CUST-MIDDLE-NAME, and CUST-LAST-NAME are populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program formats the customer's full name for the statement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CUST-FIRST-NAME delimited by space, followed by a single space, followed by CUST-MIDDLE-NAME delimited by space, followed by a single space, followed by CUST-LAST-NAME delimited by space, followed by a single space, are concatenated into ST-NAME

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Customer Full Name by Concatenating Name Components
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's full name is constructed by concatenating the first name, middle name, and last name components with single space separators. Each name component is delimited by a space character to exclude trailing spaces, producing a compact formatted name string.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: Customer record has been retrieved and CUST-ADDR-LINE-1, CUST-ADDR-LINE-2, CUST-ADDR-LINE-3, CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD, CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD, and CUST-ADDR-ZIP are populated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program formats the customer address for the statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Customer Address Lines for Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's mailing address is formatted for the statement. Address lines 1 and 2 are copied directly from the customer record. Address line 3 is constructed by combining the city, state code, country code, and ZIP code into a single formatted string.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Plain Text Statement Header with Customer and Account Details
all_rules.Rule_Description: The plain text account statement header is written to STMT-FILE containing the statement banner, formatted customer name and address, account ID, current balance, and FICO credit score. Multiple formatted lines are written to establish the statement structure.

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write HTML Basic Account Details Section
