Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The in-memory transaction table is populated with card groups indexed by CR-JMP from 1 to CR-CNT, and XREF-CARD-NUM from the current cross-reference record is available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program searches the in-memory table for transactions matching the current card number
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CR-JMP iterates from 1 through CR-CNT; if WS-CARD-NUM(CR-JMP) is greater than XREF-CARD-NUM, the search loop terminates immediately; if WS-CARD-NUM(CR-JMP) equals XREF-CARD-NUM, all transactions for that card group are processed by iterating TR-JMP from 1 through WS-TRCT(CR-JMP), moving WS-CARD-NUM(CR-JMP) to TRNX-CARD-NUM, WS-TRAN-NUM(CR-JMP, TR-JMP) to TRNX-ID, and WS-TRAN-REST(CR-JMP, TR-JMP) to TRNX-REST for each transaction

all_rules.Rule_Name: Match Card Number and Retrieve All Transactions for Current Account
all_rules.Rule_Description: The in-memory transaction table is searched to find all transactions belonging to the card number from the current cross-reference record. The search iterates through the table and stops early if the table card number exceeds the XREF card number, assuming the table is in sorted order.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A matching transaction has been found in the in-memory table with TRNX-ID, TRNX-DESC (from TRNX-REST), and TRNX-AMT (from TRNX-REST) available
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the individual transaction details
Acceptance_Criteria.Then:
TRNX-ID is moved to ST-TRANID, TRNX-DESC is moved to ST-TRANDT, TRNX-AMT is moved to ST-TRANAMT; ST-LINE14 containing ST-TRANID, ST-TRANDT, and ST-TRANAMT is written to FD-STMTFILE-REC; for HTML-FILE, HTML-LTRS (row start) and HTML-L58 (cell start) are written, then HTML-TRAN-LN is constructed by concatenating '

' with ST-TRANID and '

' and written; HTML-LTDE (cell end) and HTML-L61 (next cell) are written, then HTML-TRAN-LN with ST-TRANDT is written; HTML-LTDE and HTML-L64 (next cell) are written, then HTML-TRAN-LN with ST-TRANAMT is written; HTML-LTDE and HTML-LTRE (row end) are written to close the transaction row

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Individual Transaction Line to Plain Text and HTML Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each individual transaction is written to both the plain text statement file and the HTML statement file. The transaction details include the Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been written to the statement files and TRNX-AMT contains the current transaction's amount; WS-TOTAL-AMT holds the accumulated total for the current statement
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program accumulates the transaction amount into the running total
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: TRNX-AMT is added to WS-TOTAL-AMT; this accumulation occurs for every transaction processed within the current card's transaction group

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accumulate Running Total of Transaction Amounts per Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: As each transaction is processed for a customer account statement, its amount is added to a running total. This total represents the sum of all transaction amounts for the current account statement and is reset to zero before each new statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transactions for the current card have been written and WS-TOTAL-AMT contains the sum of all transaction amounts for the current statement
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the statement total and footer to STMT-FILE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: WS-TOTAL-AMT is moved to WS-TRN-AMT; WS-TRN-AMT is moved to ST-TOTAL-TRAMT; ST-LINE12 (separator line) is written to FD-STMTFILE-REC; ST-LINE14A (total amount line containing ST-TOTAL-TRAMT) is written; ST-LINE15 (end-of-statement banner) is written to complete the plain text statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Statement Total Amount and Plain Text Footer
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all transactions for a card have been written, the accumulated total transaction amount is formatted and written as the statement summary total, followed by end-of-statement footer lines in the plain text statement file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transaction rows and the total amount have been written to HTML-FILE for the current customer account statement
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program writes the HTML statement footer
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: HTML-LTRS (table row start) is written to FD-HTMLFILE-REC; HTML-L10 (table data start) is written; HTML-L75 (end-of-statement marker content) is written; HTML-LTDE (table data end) is written; HTML-LTRE (table row end) is written; HTML-L78, HTML-L79, and HTML-L80 (closing HTML structural tags) are written to complete and close the HTML document

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write HTML Statement Footer and Closing Tags
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all transactions and the total amount have been written, the HTML statement is closed with an end-of-statement marker and the appropriate HTML closing structure tags.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new cross-reference record has been read and customer and account information has been retrieved; the statement header has been written
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program prepares to process transactions for the new account statement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: WS-TOTAL-AMT is set to ZERO before the transaction retrieval and accumulation loop begins for the current card number; CR-JMP is set to 1 as the starting index for the transaction table search

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Total Transaction Amount Before Processing Next Account Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before processing transactions for each new customer account statement, the running total transaction amount is reset to zero to ensure that the total reflects only the transactions belonging to the current statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The main processing loop has completed because XREFFILE has reached end-of-file and all customer account statements have been generated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program closes all files
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: TRNXFILE is closed by calling CBSTM03B with DD name 'TRNXFILE' and operation M03B-CLOSE; XREFFILE is closed by calling CBSTM03B with DD name 'XREFFILE' and operation M03B-CLOSE; CUSTFILE is closed by calling CBSTM03B with DD name 'CUSTFILE' and operation M03B-CLOSE; ACCTFILE is closed by calling CBSTM03B with DD name 'ACCTFILE' and operation M03B-CLOSE; STMT-FILE and HTML-FILE are closed together; the program then terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close All Input and Output Files at End of Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all cross-reference records have been processed and all statements have been generated, all input and output files are closed in sequence to finalize the output and release file resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed its startup display of job and DD name information and is ready to begin output file preparation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its output files at the start of processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The plain text statement file (STMT-FILE) is opened in output mode and is ready to receive formatted account statement records for all customers to be processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Plain Text Statement File for Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any customer statement processing begins, the plain text statement output file (STMT-FILE) must be opened in output mode to receive formatted account statement records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed its startup display of job and DD name information and is ready to begin output file preparation
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program initializes its output files at the start of processing
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The HTML statement file (HTML-FILE) is opened in output mode and is ready to receive HTML-formatted account statement records for all customers to be processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open HTML Statement File for Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before any customer statement processing begins, the HTML-formatted statement output file (HTML-FILE) must be opened in output mode to receive HTML-structured account statement records.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is at the output file initialization stage prior to any customer statement processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The output file initialization step is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both STMT-FILE and HTML-FILE are opened for output in the same operation, ensuring that both plain text and HTML statement formats are available before the first customer record is processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Simultaneous Opening of Both Statement Output Files
all_rules.Rule_Description: Both the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE) and the HTML statement file (HTML-FILE) must be opened together in a single operation before any customer processing begins, ensuring both output channels are available simultaneously for dual-format statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is at the initialization stage before transaction data loading and customer statement processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction table initialization step is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire transaction table (WS-TRNX-TABLE) is cleared of all data — all card numbers, transaction IDs, transaction details, and transaction amounts stored in the table are reset to their initial empty state, ensuring no residual data exists before new transaction records are loaded

all_rules.Rule_Name: Clear Transaction Table Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The in-memory transaction table (WS-TRNX-TABLE), which will hold all pre-loaded transaction records grouped by card number, must be fully cleared and reset to empty before any transaction data is loaded or any customer processing begins.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is at the initialization stage before transaction data loading and customer statement processing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction counter initialization step is executed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire transaction counter structure (WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR) is reset to zero — all card group counters and per-card transaction count trackers are set to zero, ensuring accurate counting when transaction records are subsequently loaded into the transaction table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Transaction Counter Structures Before Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction counter structure (WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR), which tracks the number of unique card groups and the number of transactions per card group in the in-memory table, must be fully reset to zero before any transaction data is loaded.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has just started execution and displayed job identification and DD name information
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program proceeds to the file opening and transaction loading sequence
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: All four initialization steps must have been completed in order: (1) STMT-FILE opened for output, (2) HTML-FILE opened for output, (3) WS-TRNX-TABLE cleared of all data, and (4) WS-TRN-TBL-CNTR reset to zero — only after all four steps are complete does the program proceed to open transaction, cross-reference, customer, and account files

all_rules.Rule_Name: Output File and Table Initialization Must Precede All Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: The complete initialization sequence — opening both output files and clearing the transaction table and counters — must be fully completed before any file opening, transaction loading, or customer statement generation activity begins. This ensures a clean and consistent starting state for all downstream processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction file (TRNXFILE) is available and the file access module (CBSTM03B) is ready to be called
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the file access module to open the transaction file with an OPEN operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction file is successfully opened and the system proceeds to read the first transaction record; if the file cannot be opened, the program terminates abnormally with an error message indicating the transaction file could not be opened

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Transaction File Before Loading
all_rules.Rule_Description: The transaction file must be successfully opened before any transaction records can be read and loaded into the in-memory table. The system invokes the file access module to open the transaction file and verifies the operation was successful before proceeding.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction file (TRNXFILE) has been successfully opened and contains at least one transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system reads the first transaction record from the transaction file using the file access module (CBSTM03B)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The first transaction record is loaded into the transaction record area (TRNX-RECORD); the card number from that record (TRNX-CARD-NUM) is saved as the reference card number (WS-SAVE-CARD); the card group counter (CR-CNT) is initialized to 1; and the transaction counter (TR-CNT) is initialized to 0, preparing the system to begin the transaction loading loop

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read First Transaction Record and Initialize Card Group and Transaction Counters
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the transaction file is opened, the first transaction record is read and used to initialize the card group tracking variables. The card number from the first record is saved as the reference card number, the card group counter is set to 1, and the transaction counter is set to 0 to prepare for the loading loop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the transaction file and the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD) is available for comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system compares the current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) against the saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card numbers are equal, the transaction is treated as belonging to the current card group and the transaction counter is incremented; if the card numbers differ, the transaction is treated as the first transaction of a new card group, triggering the card group transition logic

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Whether Current Transaction Belongs to Same or New Card Group
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction record processed during the loading loop, the system determines whether the transaction belongs to the current card group or starts a new card group by comparing the current transaction's card number against the previously saved card number.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) matches the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD), indicating the transaction belongs to the current card group
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the card numbers are equal
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction counter (TR-CNT) is incremented by 1, reflecting that one additional transaction belongs to the current card group

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Transaction Counter for Current Card Group When Same Card Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction record has the same card number as the previously processed record, it belongs to the current card group. The transaction counter for the current card group is incremented by 1 to track how many transactions are associated with this card.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) does not match the previously saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD), indicating a new card group is starting
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the card number change
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction count (TR-CNT) is saved into the transaction count array (WS-TRCT) at the current card group position (CR-CNT), preserving the count for the completed card group; the card group counter (CR-CNT) is incremented by 1 to move to the next card group slot; and the transaction counter (TR-CNT) is reset to 1 to count the first transaction of the new card group

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transition to New Card Group When Different Card Number Detected
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction record has a different card number from the previously processed record, it signals the start of a new card group. The system finalizes the current card group by saving its transaction count, advances the card group counter to the next position, and resets the transaction counter to 1 for the new card group.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card group counter (CR-CNT) and transaction counter (TR-CNT) have been updated to reflect the correct position for the current transaction in the in-memory table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the current transaction's data into the in-memory transaction table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) is stored in the card number array (WS-CARD-NUM) at position CR-CNT; the transaction ID (TRNX-ID) is stored in the transaction number array (WS-TRAN-NUM) at position [CR-CNT, TR-CNT]; and all remaining transaction details (TRNX-REST, which includes transaction description, amount, and other fields) are stored in the transaction details array (WS-TRAN-REST) at position [CR-CNT, TR-CNT]

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Transaction Data in Two-Dimensional In-Memory Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the card group and transaction counters are updated, the current transaction's data is stored in the two-dimensional in-memory table. The card number is stored at the card group level, while the transaction ID and all remaining transaction details are stored at the specific card group and transaction position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current transaction record has been stored in the in-memory table at the correct card group and transaction position
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system updates the card number reference for the next comparison
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD) is updated to the current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM), so that the next transaction read from the file can be compared against this value to determine card group membership

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Saved Card Number After Storing Transaction
all_rules.Rule_Description: After storing the current transaction in the in-memory table, the saved card number reference is updated to the current transaction's card number. This ensures the next transaction can be correctly compared to determine whether it belongs to the same or a new card group.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current transaction has been stored in the in-memory table and the saved card number has been updated
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the file access module (CBSTM03B) to read the next sequential record from the transaction file (TRNXFILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a record is successfully retrieved, it is loaded into the transaction record area (TRNX-RECORD) and the loading loop continues by returning to the card number comparison step; if the end of the transaction file is reached, the system proceeds to finalize the last card group; if any other read failure occurs, the program terminates abnormally with an error message indicating the transaction file could not be read

all_rules.Rule_Name: Read Next Transaction Record from Transaction File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After storing the current transaction and updating the saved card number, the system reads the next sequential transaction record from the transaction file to continue the loading loop. The file access module is invoked with a READ operation and the result determines whether processing continues or the end-of-file condition is reached.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A read operation has been performed on the transaction file (TRNXFILE) via the file access module (CBSTM03B)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the return status from the file access module
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the return status indicates a successful read (return code '00'), the newly read record is placed into the transaction record area (TRNX-RECORD) and the loop continues back to the card number comparison; if the return status indicates end of file (return code '10'), the system proceeds to save the final transaction count for the last card group and concludes the loading process

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect End of Transaction File to Finalize Loading
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each read attempt, the system evaluates the result to determine whether more transaction records are available or whether the end of the transaction file has been reached, which signals that the loading process is complete.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The end of the transaction file has been reached and the last card group's transactions have all been stored in the in-memory table but the final transaction count has not yet been saved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system detects the end-of-file condition and executes the finalization step
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction counter value (TR-CNT) is saved into the transaction count array (WS-TRCT) at the current card group position (CR-CNT), ensuring the last card group's transaction count is correctly recorded; the in-memory transaction table is now fully populated with all card groups and their associated transactions, and the system proceeds to open the next required file (XREFFILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Final Transaction Count for Last Card Group at End of File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the transaction file is reached, the transaction count for the last card group has not yet been saved (since the save normally occurs when a new card number is detected). The system must explicitly save the transaction count for the last card group to ensure it is correctly recorded in the in-memory table.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File (TRNXFILE) has been successfully opened and the first transaction record has been read
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The first transaction record is available with a Card Number
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card Number from the first transaction record is saved as the current reference card number (WS-SAVE-CARD), the unique card counter (CR-CNT) is set to 1, and the transaction counter (TR-CNT) is set to 0

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Transaction Grouping with First Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Transaction File is opened and the first transaction record is successfully read, the grouping process is initialized by saving the first card number as the reference card, setting the unique card counter to 1, and setting the transaction counter to 0 in preparation for grouping.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read from the Transaction File and a saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD) exists from the previous transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card number of the current transaction record (TRNX-CARD-NUM) is compared to the saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the card numbers match, the transaction is treated as belonging to the same card group; if the card numbers differ, the transaction is treated as the start of a new card group

all_rules.Rule_Name: Detect Card Number Change to Identify New Card Group
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction record being processed during the pre-load phase, the program compares the current transaction's card number against the previously saved card number to determine whether the transaction belongs to the same card group or starts a new card group.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read and the current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) matches the saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card number match is confirmed
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The transaction counter (TR-CNT) is incremented by 1 to reflect the additional transaction under the current card group

all_rules.Rule_Name: Increment Transaction Count for Same Card Group
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction record's card number matches the previously saved card number, it is identified as belonging to the current card group, and the transaction counter for that group is incremented by 1.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been read and the current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) does NOT match the saved card number (WS-SAVE-CARD)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: A card number change is detected
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction count (TR-CNT) is saved as the transaction count for the previous card group at position WS-TRCT(CR-CNT), the unique card counter (CR-CNT) is incremented by 1, and the transaction counter (TR-CNT) is reset to 1 for the new card group

all_rules.Rule_Name: Start New Card Group When Card Number Changes
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a transaction record's card number differs from the previously saved card number, the current card group is closed by saving its transaction count, the unique card counter is incremented to start a new card group, and the transaction counter is reset to 1 for the new card group.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card group index (CR-CNT) and transaction index (TR-CNT) have been determined for the current transaction record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction details are stored in the in-memory table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) is stored at WS-CARD-NUM(CR-CNT), the transaction ID (TRNX-ID) is stored at WS-TRAN-NUM(CR-CNT, TR-CNT), and all remaining transaction details including description and amount (TRNX-REST) are stored at WS-TRAN-REST(CR-CNT, TR-CNT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Store Transaction Details Under Current Card Group
all_rules.Rule_Description: After determining the card group (same or new), the transaction's card number, transaction ID, and all remaining transaction details (including description and amount) are stored in the in-memory transaction table at the position corresponding to the current card group index and transaction index.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current transaction's details have been stored in the in-memory table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction storage step is complete
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The saved card number reference (WS-SAVE-CARD) is updated to the current transaction's card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Update Saved Card Number to Current Transaction Card Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: After storing the transaction details, the saved card number reference is updated to the current transaction's card number so that the next transaction can be correctly compared to detect card group changes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current transaction record has been processed and stored in the in-memory table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The next transaction record is read from the Transaction File (TRNXFILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If a record is successfully read (return code '00'), the transaction details are moved to TRNX-RECORD and the grouping loop continues from the card number comparison step; if end-of-file is reached (return code '10'), the loop exits to finalize the last card group

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Reading Transaction Records Until End of File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After processing each transaction record, the program reads the next transaction record from the Transaction File and continues the grouping loop. The loop continues until all transaction records have been read, at which point the end-of-file condition terminates the loading phase.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The end of the Transaction File has been reached and the last card group's transactions have been stored in the in-memory table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: No more transaction records are available to read
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The final transaction count (TR-CNT) is saved as the transaction count for the last card group at position WS-TRCT(CR-CNT), completing the in-memory transaction table and making it ready for statement processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Save Final Transaction Count for Last Card Group at End of File
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the end of the Transaction File is reached, the transaction count accumulated for the last card group must be explicitly saved into the in-memory table, as there is no subsequent card number change to trigger the automatic save that occurs for all preceding card groups.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program has completed loading all transaction records into memory and is ready to begin opening the reference data files
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program requests to open the Card-to-Customer/Account Cross-Reference File by calling the file management service (CBSTM03B) with the file identifier set to 'XREFFILE' and the operation set to OPEN
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file management service attempts to open the Cross-Reference File and returns a result indicating whether the file was successfully opened or not

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke Cross-Reference File Open Service
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the program is ready to open the Cross-Reference File, it must invoke the external file management service (CBSTM03B) with the XREFFILE identifier and an OPEN operation request to make the card-to-customer and card-to-account cross-reference data available for lookup.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file management service has been called to open the Cross-Reference File (XREFFILE) and has returned a result code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program evaluates the result of the open request — a result of 'Successful' (return codes '00' or '04') indicates the file is ready, while any other result indicates the file could not be opened
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the file opened successfully, the Cross-Reference File is marked as ready and processing continues to open the Customer File next; if the file could not be opened, an error message 'ERROR OPENING XREFFILE' is displayed along with the specific return code received, and all processing is stopped immediately

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Cross-Reference File Open Result
all_rules.Rule_Description: After requesting to open the Cross-Reference File, the program must evaluate the result returned by the file management service. A successful open allows processing to continue; any failure result must stop all processing immediately as the cross-reference data is essential for linking card numbers to customer and account information.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference File (XREFFILE) has been successfully opened and is ready for card-to-customer and card-to-account lookups
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program registers the successful open of the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The program sets the next file to be opened as the Customer File ('CUSTFILE') and returns control to the file-opening dispatcher to continue the file opening sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Proceed to Open Customer File After Cross-Reference File is Ready
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the Cross-Reference File has been successfully opened and is ready for use, the program must immediately proceed to open the Customer File as the next step in the mandatory file opening sequence. The Customer File must be opened before any customer data lookups can be performed during statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file opening sequence has completed opening TRNXFILE and XREFFILE, and the system is ready to open the customer master file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to open the customer data source
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must designate 'CUSTFILE' as the target file, set the operation mode to OPEN, and reset the return status to zero before invoking the file open service

all_rules.Rule_Name: Select Customer File as Target for Customer Data Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before opening the customer file, the system must designate CUSTFILE as the target data source and set the operation mode to OPEN, ensuring the correct file is identified for all subsequent customer demographic and address lookups by Customer ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: CUSTFILE has been designated as the target file, the operation mode is set to OPEN, and the return status has been reset to zero
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system calls the external file access service 'CBSTM03B' with the file control area (WS-M03B-AREA) containing the CUSTFILE open request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The external service attempts to open CUSTFILE and returns a completion status code in the file control area for the system to evaluate

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open Customer Master File via File Access Service
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system must invoke the external file access service module (CBSTM03B) to physically open the customer master file (CUSTFILE), passing the prepared file control area containing the target file name and open operation request.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external file access service 'CBSTM03B' has been called to open CUSTFILE and has returned a completion status code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the return status code from the CUSTFILE open request
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the return status is '00' (open successful) or '04' (open successful with warning), the system considers CUSTFILE successfully opened and proceeds to the next step in the file opening sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Successful Opening of Customer File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After requesting the customer file to be opened, the system must evaluate the return status from the file access service. A return status of '00' (successful open) or '04' (successful open with warning) are both treated as successful outcomes, allowing processing to continue.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external file access service 'CBSTM03B' has been called to open CUSTFILE and has returned a completion status code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The return status code is anything other than '00' or '04'
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the message 'ERROR OPENING CUSTFILE', display the actual return status code received, and immediately terminate the program abnormally — no further customer statements are produced

all_rules.Rule_Name: Terminate Processing on Customer File Open Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the customer master file cannot be opened for any reason other than a successful or warning status, the system must immediately display a descriptive error message identifying the failed file and stop all processing. This prevents any customer statement generation from proceeding without access to customer demographic data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: CUSTFILE has been successfully opened with a return status of '00' or '04' and is ready to serve customer demographic and address data lookups by Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the successful open of CUSTFILE
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must set the next target file to 'ACCTFILE' and transfer control to the file opening dispatcher (0000-START) to continue the mandatory file opening sequence with the Account File

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer File Ready — Proceed to Open Account File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once CUSTFILE is confirmed as successfully opened, it becomes available for keyed lookups by Customer ID throughout the main processing loop. The system must then immediately proceed to the next mandatory step in the file opening sequence: opening the Account File (ACCTFILE). All four files must be open before customer statement generation can begin.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system has completed opening the Customer File and is ready to enable account data retrieval, and the Account Master File (ACCTFILE) has not yet been opened
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the file access service (CBSTM03B) to open the Account Master File (ACCTFILE) in read mode
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file access service (CBSTM03B) is called with the file identifier set to 'ACCTFILE' and the operation set to OPEN, so that account balance and credit score data becomes accessible by account ID

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke Account File Open Service
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the system needs to access account balance and credit score information, it must invoke the file access service (CBSTM03B) to open the Account Master File (ACCTFILE) before any account data retrieval can occur.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file access service (CBSTM03B) has been called to open the Account Master File (ACCTFILE) and has returned a response
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the response from the file access service
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the response indicates normal completion or an at-open end-of-file condition, the Account Master File is considered successfully opened and the system proceeds to main statement processing; otherwise, the system displays the message 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE' along with the returned response code, and terminates processing abnormally

all_rules.Rule_Name: Validate Account File Opened Successfully
all_rules.Rule_Description: After requesting the Account Master File to be opened, the system must verify whether the file was successfully opened. A successful open is indicated by a normal completion or an end-of-file-at-open condition. Any other outcome is treated as a failure and halts processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File (ACCTFILE) has been successfully opened and is available for keyed retrieval of account balance and credit score data
Acceptance_Criteria.When: All four required files (Transaction File, Cross-Reference File, Customer File, and Account File) have been successfully opened
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system proceeds directly to the main statement processing loop, where it will read cross-reference records and retrieve account balance and FICO credit score information from the Account Master File using the account ID as the lookup key

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account File Ready for Statement Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once the Account Master File is confirmed as successfully opened, the system is ready to retrieve account balance and FICO credit score information by account ID, and main statement generation processing can begin.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference File (XREFFILE) has been opened and is positioned at the next unread record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system requests the next sequential record from the Cross-Reference File by calling the file access service CBSTM03B with the file identifier set to 'XREFFILE' and the operation mode set to sequential read
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The file access service is invoked and returns either a record with its data or an end-of-file signal or an error condition

all_rules.Rule_Name: Invoke Cross-Reference File Sequential Read Service
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program invokes an external file access service (CBSTM03B) to sequentially read the next record from the Cross-Reference File, which links card numbers to customer IDs and account IDs for statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file access service has successfully read a record from the Cross-Reference File and the read operation returned a successful status (return code '00')
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record data returned by the file access service is available in the file data field (WS-M03B-FLDT)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The record data is mapped into the Cross-Reference Record structure (CARD-XREF-RECORD), making the Card Number, Customer ID, and Account ID available for downstream processing including customer data retrieval, account data retrieval, and statement creation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Extract Cross-Reference Data from Successfully Read Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a Cross-Reference record is successfully retrieved, the system extracts the Card Number, Customer ID, and Account ID from the record data to be used for subsequent customer and account lookups and statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The file access service has been called to read the next record from the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file access service returns an end-of-file condition (return code '10'), indicating there are no more Cross-Reference records available
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The End-of-File flag (END-OF-FILE) is set to 'Y', which will cause the main processing loop to terminate and prevent any further customer, account, or transaction lookups and statement generation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set End-of-File Flag When Cross-Reference Records Are Exhausted
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the Cross-Reference File has no more records to deliver, the system sets an end-of-file indicator to signal that all customer-account-card relationships have been processed and statement generation should stop.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The main processing loop is active and the End-of-File flag (END-OF-FILE) is currently set to 'N', indicating unprocessed Cross-Reference records remain
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system evaluates the loop continuation condition at the start of each iteration
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the End-of-File flag is 'N', the system proceeds to read the next Cross-Reference record and, if the read is also successful (End-of-File remains 'N' after the read), continues to retrieve customer data, retrieve account data, create the statement, reset the transaction total to zero, and retrieve and write transactions; if the End-of-File flag is 'Y' at any check point, the loop terminates and no further statement processing occurs

all_rules.Rule_Name: Continue Main Processing Loop While Cross-Reference Records Exist
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Cross-Reference File drives the entire statement generation process. The main processing loop continues to read Cross-Reference records sequentially and generate statements only while the end-of-file flag has not been set, ensuring one complete statement cycle per Cross-Reference record.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully read from the Cross-Reference File
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The record data is mapped into the Cross-Reference Record structure (CARD-XREF-RECORD)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The following three data elements become available for the current statement cycle: the Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) used to match transactions from the pre-loaded transaction table, the Customer ID (XREF-CUST-ID) used as the key to retrieve the customer's personal and address information, and the Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID) used as the key to retrieve the account's balance and financial details

all_rules.Rule_Name: Definitional Mapping of Cross-Reference Record Fields
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Cross-Reference record is the authoritative source that defines the relationship between a Card Number, a Customer ID, and an Account ID. Each record in the Cross-Reference File represents one unique card-to-customer-to-account association used to drive statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully read and is available for processing, containing a Customer ID field (XREF-CUST-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to retrieve customer information from the Customer Master File
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer ID value from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CUST-ID) must be used as the exact lookup key, and the full length of the Customer ID must be computed and passed as the key length for the lookup

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer ID Sourced from Cross-Reference Record as Lookup Key
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Customer ID used to retrieve customer information must always originate from the current Cross-Reference record being processed, ensuring each customer lookup is driven by the cross-reference data.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer ID from the Cross-Reference record has been set as the lookup key and the Customer Master File (CUSTFILE) is open and accessible
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the external file access module CBSTM03B with a keyed-read operation targeting the Customer Master File using the Customer ID as the search key
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The external module CBSTM03B must be called with the Customer Master File identifier, the keyed-read mode flag set, and the Customer ID and its computed length as the lookup key parameters

all_rules.Rule_Name: Key-Based Direct Lookup into Customer Master File via External Module
all_rules.Rule_Description: Customer information must be retrieved using a direct key-based read operation against the Customer Master File, delegated to the external file access module CBSTM03B, ensuring precise single-record retrieval by Customer ID.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external file access module CBSTM03B has been called to perform a keyed read on the Customer Master File using the Customer ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The module returns a response code indicating the outcome of the lookup
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the response code is '00' (success), processing continues normally; if the response code is anything other than '00' (record not found, file error, or any other condition), the system must display the message 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' and immediately abort all processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Successful Customer Record Retrieval Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Customer Master File lookup is performed, the system must validate whether the customer record was successfully found. Only a successful retrieval (return code '00') allows processing to continue; any other outcome must immediately abort all processing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external file access module CBSTM03B has successfully retrieved the customer record (response code '00') and the customer data is held in the module's output data field
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system stores the retrieved customer data for use in statement generation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The entire customer record returned by the module must be moved into the CUSTOMER-RECORD working storage area, populating all customer fields including First Name, Middle Name, Last Name, Address Line 1, Address Line 2, Address Line 3, State Code, Country Code, Zip Code, and FICO Credit Score

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Record Storage for Statement Generation
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful retrieval, the complete customer record returned by the file access module must be stored in the Customer Record working area, making all customer data fields available for subsequent statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved and stored, containing First Name (CUST-FIRST-NAME), Middle Name (CUST-MIDDLE-NAME), and Last Name (CUST-LAST-NAME) fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the customer name for statement generation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full name must be constructed by concatenating First Name, a single space, Middle Name, a single space, and Last Name — each name component delimited by a space character — and stored in the statement name field (ST-NAME)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Full Name Construction for Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's full name must be constructed by concatenating the First Name, Middle Name, and Last Name fields from the retrieved customer record, with each name component separated by a single space, for use in the account statement output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved and stored, containing Address Line 1 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-1) and Address Line 2 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-2)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares customer address information for statement generation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Address Line 1 from the customer record must be directly assigned to statement address field ST-ADD1, and Address Line 2 must be directly assigned to statement address field ST-ADD2, with no transformation applied

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Address Lines 1 and 2 Assignment for Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first two lines of the customer's address must be directly copied from the customer record into the corresponding statement address fields for output in both the plain-text and HTML statement formats.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved and stored, containing Address Line 3 (CUST-ADDR-LINE-3), State Code (CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD), Country Code (CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD), and Zip Code (CUST-ADDR-ZIP)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the combined city-state-country-zip address line for statement generation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The combined address line must be constructed by concatenating Address Line 3, a single space, State Code, a single space, Country Code, a single space, and Zip Code — each component delimited by a space character — and stored in statement address field ST-ADD3

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer Address Line 3 Construction with State, Country, and Zip Code
all_rules.Rule_Description: The third address line displayed on the customer statement must be constructed by concatenating the city (Address Line 3), State Code, Country Code, and Zip Code from the customer record, each separated by a single space.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer record has been successfully retrieved and stored, containing the FICO Credit Score field (CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares customer financial information for statement generation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The FICO Credit Score value from the customer record (CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE) must be directly assigned to the statement FICO score field (ST-FICO-SCORE) for inclusion in the generated statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Customer FICO Credit Score Assignment for Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's FICO credit score retrieved from the Customer Master File must be assigned to the statement output field so it is included in both the plain-text and HTML versions of the account statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The external file access module CBSTM03B has been called to retrieve a customer record using the Customer ID from the Cross-Reference record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The module returns any response code other than '00' (successful retrieval), indicating the customer record was not found or a file access error occurred
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must display the error message 'ERROR READING CUSTFILE' and immediately invoke the abnormal termination process, halting all further processing without generating any statement output for the current or subsequent customers

all_rules.Rule_Name: Immediate Processing Abort on Customer Retrieval Failure
all_rules.Rule_Description: If the customer record cannot be retrieved for any reason — including record not found or any file access error — the entire program must be immediately terminated to prevent generation of incomplete or inaccurate customer statements.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A cross-reference record has been successfully read and contains a valid Account ID (XREF-ACCT-ID)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system initiates a keyed read operation against the Account Master File (ACCTFILE) using the Account ID from the cross-reference record as the search key, with the key length computed from the Account ID field size
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Master File is searched using the Account ID as the exact lookup key, and the keyed read request is submitted to the file access service (CBSTM03B) targeting the ACCTFILE data source

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Lookup Key Preparation from Cross-Reference Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system extracts the Account ID from the current cross-reference record and uses it as the exact-match key to perform a direct keyed lookup against the Account Master File via the CBSTM03B file access module.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A keyed read request has been submitted to the Account Master File using the Account ID from the cross-reference record
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The file access service (CBSTM03B) returns a response after attempting to locate the account record
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the account record is found successfully (return code = '00'), processing continues normally; if the account record is not found or any other error condition is returned (any return code other than '00'), an error message 'ERROR READING ACCTFILE' is displayed along with the return code received, and the program immediately stops all processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Record Found Validation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the keyed lookup is performed against the Account Master File, the system validates whether the account record was successfully retrieved. If the account is not found or any retrieval error occurs, processing is immediately halted.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Master File keyed lookup has completed successfully with a return code of '00'
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system maps the retrieved raw account data from the file access service response area into the Account Record structure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Record is populated with all account details returned from the Account Master File, including Account ID and Current Balance, ready for use in statement generation

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Details Retrieval into Account Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Upon successful retrieval from the Account Master File, the raw account data returned by the file access service is mapped into the structured Account Record, making the account details available for downstream statement generation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Account Record has been successfully populated with account data from the Account Master File, containing Account ID (ACCT-ID) and Current Balance (ACCT-CURR-BAL)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the statement data fields for output generation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account ID from the Account Record is placed into the statement Account ID field (ST-ACCT-ID), and the Current Balance from the Account Record is placed into the statement Current Balance field (ST-CURR-BAL), making both values available for inclusion in the customer statement output in both plain-text and HTML formats

all_rules.Rule_Name: Account Details Made Available for Statement Generation
all_rules.Rule_Description: The account details retrieved from the Account Master File — specifically the Account ID and Current Balance — are transferred into the statement data fields so they can be included in both the plain-text and HTML-formatted customer account statements.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Customer Record is available containing a Customer First Name, Customer Middle Name, and Customer Last Name, and a statement is being prepared for that customer
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system formats the customer's full name for display on the account statement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system must: (1) Take the Customer First Name from the Customer Record and strip any trailing spaces from it; (2) Append a single space after the First Name; (3) Append the Customer Middle Name from the Customer Record, stripping any trailing spaces from it; (4) Append a single space after the Middle Name; (5) Append the Customer Last Name from the Customer Record, stripping any trailing spaces from it; (6) Append a single trailing space after the Last Name; (7) Store the fully concatenated name string into the Statement Name Field (ST-NAME), which is then used for display on both the plain-text statement and the HTML-formatted statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format Customer Full Name for Statement Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: When generating a customer account statement, the customer's full name must be constructed by combining the first name, middle name, and last name from the Customer Record into a single formatted name string, with a single space separating each name component. Trailing spaces within each individual name part are removed before concatenation. The resulting full name is stored in the Statement Name Field for display on both the plain-text and HTML versions of the statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer File using the Customer ID from the Cross-Reference record, and the customer record contains a value in Address Line 1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the customer address section of the account statement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The value of Address Line 1 from the customer record is copied exactly as-is into Statement Address Field 1 (ST-ADD1), with no formatting or transformation applied

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Customer Primary Address Line to Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Address Line 1 from the customer record is directly copied into the first address field of the customer statement without any transformation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer File using the Customer ID from the Cross-Reference record, and the customer record contains a value in Address Line 2
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the customer address section of the account statement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The value of Address Line 2 from the customer record is copied exactly as-is into Statement Address Field 2 (ST-ADD2), with no formatting or transformation applied

all_rules.Rule_Name: Copy Customer Secondary Address Line to Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Address Line 2 from the customer record is directly copied into the second address field of the customer statement without any transformation.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been successfully retrieved from the Customer File using the Customer ID from the Cross-Reference record, and the customer record contains values for Address Line 3 (city), State Code, Country Code, and ZIP Code
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares the combined city-state-country-zip address line for the account statement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The system constructs Statement Address Field 3 (ST-ADD3) by concatenating the following components in order, each separated by a single space: (1) Address Line 3 truncated at the first space, (2) State Code truncated at the first space, (3) Country Code truncated at the first space, (4) ZIP Code truncated at the first space — resulting in a single formatted address string stored in ST-ADD3

all_rules.Rule_Name: Format and Combine Customer City, State, Country and ZIP into Statement Address Line 3
all_rules.Rule_Description: Address Line 3 (city), State Code, Country Code, and ZIP Code from the customer record are combined into a single space-separated formatted string for the third address field of the customer statement. Each component is trimmed at its first space boundary before being joined.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new customer statement is being generated for a customer-account combination retrieved from the cross-reference file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The plain text statement header writing process begins
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The opening banner line (ST-LINE0) is written as the first record to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE), marking the start of a new customer statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Start-of-Statement Banner to Plain Text File
all_rules.Rule_Description: At the beginning of each customer statement generation cycle, an opening banner line is written to the plain text statement file to mark the start of a new statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been retrieved containing CUST-FIRST-NAME, CUST-MIDDLE-NAME, and CUST-LAST-NAME fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The customer full name is being prepared for the plain text statement header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full name is constructed by concatenating CUST-FIRST-NAME (delimited by space), a single space, CUST-MIDDLE-NAME (delimited by space), a single space, and CUST-LAST-NAME (delimited by space) into the ST-NAME field; the resulting formatted full name line (ST-LINE1) is then written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build and Write Customer Full Name to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's full name is constructed by concatenating the first name, middle name, and last name from the customer record, each separated by a single space, and written to the plain text statement file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been retrieved containing CUST-ADDR-LINE-1
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The address section of the plain text statement header is being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CUST-ADDR-LINE-1 is moved to ST-ADD1, and the address line 1 record (ST-LINE2) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Customer Street Address Line 1 to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The first line of the customer's street address is copied directly from the customer record and written to the plain text statement file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been retrieved containing CUST-ADDR-LINE-2
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The address section of the plain text statement header is being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CUST-ADDR-LINE-2 is moved to ST-ADD2, and the address line 2 record (ST-LINE3) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Customer Street Address Line 2 to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The second line of the customer's street address is copied directly from the customer record and written to the plain text statement file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been retrieved containing CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 (city), CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD, CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD, and CUST-ADDR-ZIP
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The third address line is being prepared for the plain text statement header
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The combined address line 3 is constructed by concatenating CUST-ADDR-LINE-3 (delimited by space), a single space, CUST-ADDR-STATE-CD (delimited by space), a single space, CUST-ADDR-COUNTRY-CD (delimited by space), a single space, and CUST-ADDR-ZIP (delimited by space) into the ST-ADD3 field; the resulting address line 3 record (ST-LINE4) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Build and Write Customer City, State, Country, and ZIP to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The third address line is constructed by concatenating the city, state code, country code, and ZIP code from the customer record, each separated by a single space, and written to the plain text statement file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The customer address lines have been written to the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transition from the address section to the Basic Details section occurs
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A visual separator line (ST-LINE5) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE) to delineate the sections

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write First Visual Separator Line Before Basic Details Section
all_rules.Rule_Description: A visual separator line is written to the plain text statement file to visually separate the address section from the Basic Details section heading.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The first visual separator line has been written to the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Basic Details section of the statement header is being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Basic Details section label line (ST-LINE6) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Basic Details Section Heading to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: A section heading labelled 'Basic Details' is written to the plain text statement file to introduce the account and financial information section.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Basic Details section heading (ST-LINE6) has been written to the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Basic Details section heading is being framed with separators
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The same visual separator line (ST-LINE5) is written again to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE) immediately after the section heading

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Second Visual Separator Line After Basic Details Heading
all_rules.Rule_Description: A second visual separator line is written to the plain text statement file immediately after the Basic Details section heading to visually frame the heading.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been retrieved containing ACCT-ID
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Basic Details section of the plain text statement header is being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: ACCT-ID is moved to ST-ACCT-ID, and the account ID line (ST-LINE7) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set and Write Account ID to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The account identifier is retrieved from the account record and written to the plain text statement file as part of the Basic Details section.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: An account record has been retrieved containing ACCT-CURR-BAL
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Basic Details section of the plain text statement header is being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: ACCT-CURR-BAL is moved to ST-CURR-BAL, and the current balance line (ST-LINE8) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set and Write Current Account Balance to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The current account balance is retrieved from the account record and written to the plain text statement file as part of the Basic Details section.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A customer record has been retrieved containing CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The Basic Details section of the plain text statement header is being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: CUST-FICO-CREDIT-SCORE is moved to ST-FICO-SCORE, and the FICO credit score line (ST-LINE9) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set and Write Customer FICO Credit Score to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The customer's FICO credit score is retrieved from the customer record and written to the plain text statement file as part of the Basic Details section.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Basic Details section (Account ID, Current Balance, FICO Score) has been written to the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transition to the Transaction Summary section of the statement header occurs
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Summary section label line (ST-LINE10) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Transaction Summary Section Heading to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: A section heading labelled 'Transaction Summary' is written to the plain text statement file to introduce the transaction listing section.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Summary section heading has been written to the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The column header row for the transaction listing is being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The column headers line (ST-LINE11) containing labels for Transaction ID, Transaction Details, and Transaction Amount is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Transaction Column Headers to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The column header row containing the labels for Transaction ID, Transaction Details, and Transaction Amount is written to the plain text statement file to define the transaction listing columns.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction column headers (ST-LINE11) have been written to the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The separator between column headers and sub-column headers is being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A visual separator line (ST-LINE12) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write First Separator Line in Transaction Summary Section
all_rules.Rule_Description: A visual separator line is written to the plain text statement file after the column headers to visually separate the headers from the sub-column headers.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The first separator line (ST-LINE12) has been written after the main column headers in the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The sub-column header row for the transaction listing is being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The detailed sub-column labels line (ST-LINE13) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Transaction Sub-Column Headers to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: A detailed sub-column header row is written to the plain text statement file to provide more granular column labels beneath the main column headers in the transaction listing section.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The sub-column headers (ST-LINE13) have been written to the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The plain text statement header section is being finalized
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A closing visual separator line (ST-LINE12) is written to the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE), completing the statement header and marking the start of the transaction detail area

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Closing Separator Line to Complete Plain Text Statement Header
all_rules.Rule_Description: A closing visual separator line is written to the plain text statement file after the sub-column headers to complete the statement header section and mark the boundary before transaction detail lines begin.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new customer account statement is being generated and the HTML output file is open for writing
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The HTML document header writing process is initiated for a customer statement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The HTML DOCTYPE declaration line (HTML-L01) must be written as the very first line to the HTML output file, establishing the document type standard for the statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write HTML DOCTYPE Declaration to Statement Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system writes the HTML DOCTYPE declaration as the first line of the HTML statement output file, establishing the document type for the customer account statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The HTML DOCTYPE declaration has been written to the HTML output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The HTML document header writing process continues sequentially
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The opening HTML tag line (HTML-L02) must be written as the second line to the HTML output file, opening the root element of the statement document

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Opening HTML Tag to Statement Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system writes the opening HTML tag as the second line of the HTML statement output file, opening the root HTML element of the customer account statement document.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The opening HTML tag has been written to the HTML output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The HTML document header writing process continues sequentially
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The HEAD section opening tag line (HTML-L03) must be written as the third line to the HTML output file, beginning the metadata section of the statement document

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write HEAD Section Tag to Statement Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system writes the opening HEAD section tag as the third line of the HTML statement output file, beginning the document metadata section of the customer account statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The HEAD section opening tag has been written to the HTML output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The HTML document header writing process continues sequentially
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The META character encoding tag line (HTML-L04) must be written as the fourth line to the HTML output file, specifying the character encoding standard for the statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write META Character Encoding Tag to Statement Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: The system writes the META character encoding tag as the fourth line of the HTML statement output file, defining the character set used in the customer account statement document.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The META character encoding tag has been written to the HTML output file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The HTML document header writing process continues sequentially
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The TITLE tag line (HTML-L05) must be written as the fifth line to the HTML output file, providing the statement document title visible in the browser

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write TITLE Tag to Statement Output
