Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A Cross-Reference record has been successfully read, containing a Card Number (XREF-CARD-NUM) that links the customer and account to their associated transactions
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins the transaction matching process for the current customer statement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Card Number from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM) is used as the lookup key to search the in-memory transaction table for all matching transactions belonging to that card

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Card Number from Cross-Reference Record for Transaction Matching
all_rules.Rule_Description: The program uses the card number stored in the current Cross-Reference (XREF) record as the key to search the in-memory transaction table. This card number determines which pre-loaded transactions belong to the current customer statement being generated.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The program is iterating through the in-memory transaction table using a card index (CR-JMP) starting from position 1, and the total number of stored card groups is tracked by CR-CNT
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card index (CR-JMP) exceeds the total count of stored card groups (CR-CNT), OR the stored card number at the current index position (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is greater than the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The scan of the in-memory transaction table is immediately terminated and no further card entries are examined, ending the transaction matching process for the current customer statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Scan Termination Condition for In-Memory Transaction Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: The scan of the in-memory transaction table stops under two conditions: either all stored card entries have been examined, or the current stored card number is greater than the XREF card number. The second condition relies on the transaction table being in sorted order by card number, allowing early exit to avoid unnecessary scanning.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The scan of the in-memory transaction table is still active (termination conditions not yet met), and the current stored card number at index CR-JMP (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) has been retrieved
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The stored card number (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is compared against the card number from the Cross-Reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the stored card number exactly equals the XREF card number, a match is confirmed and transaction processing proceeds for that card group; if they do not match, the current card entry is skipped and the scan advances to the next stored card entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Card Number Match Verification Between XREF and In-Memory Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each card entry in the in-memory transaction table that has not yet caused a scan termination, the program checks whether the stored card number exactly matches the card number from the current Cross-Reference record. Only an exact match triggers transaction retrieval and writing.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The stored card number at the current table index (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) has been confirmed to exactly match the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The card match is confirmed and transaction processing is about to begin for this card group
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The matched card number (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is copied into the active transaction card number field (TRNX-CARD-NUM), establishing it as the card number for all transactions to be written in this processing cycle

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Active Card Number Upon Successful Match
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card number match is confirmed between the in-memory table and the Cross-Reference record, the matched card number is formally set as the active card number for the current transaction processing cycle, establishing the context for all subsequent transaction writes.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card number match has been confirmed, the matched card group is at index CR-JMP in the in-memory table, and the total number of transactions stored for that card group is recorded as WS-TRCT at CR-JMP
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program iterates through transactions using a transaction index (TR-JMP) starting from position 1 and incrementing by 1 for each transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The iteration continues processing each transaction as long as the transaction index (TR-JMP) does not exceed the stored transaction count for that card (WS-TRCT at CR-JMP); when the transaction index exceeds the count, iteration stops and the outer card scan resumes

all_rules.Rule_Name: Iterate Through All Transactions for a Matched Card
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once a card number match is found, the program iterates through every transaction stored in the in-memory table for that specific card group. The iteration continues until all transactions for that card have been processed, using the stored transaction count for that card as the upper boundary.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction iteration is active for a matched card group at card index CR-JMP, and the current transaction is at transaction index TR-JMP within that card group in the in-memory table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program retrieves the current transaction's data from the in-memory table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID stored at position (CR-JMP, TR-JMP) in the in-memory table (WS-TRAN-NUM) is copied to the active Transaction ID field (TRNX-ID), AND the full transaction details stored at position (CR-JMP, TR-JMP) in the in-memory table (WS-TRAN-REST) are copied to the active transaction details field (TRNX-REST), making both available for statement writing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Transaction ID and Details from In-Memory Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction within a matched card group, the Transaction ID and the full set of transaction details (including description, amount, date, and other attributes stored as TRNX-REST) are retrieved from the in-memory table using the combined card index and transaction index as the lookup position.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction ID (TRNX-ID) and transaction details including Description (TRNX-DESC) and Amount (TRNX-AMT) have been retrieved from the in-memory table into the active transaction fields
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction writing routine (6000-WRITE-TRANS) is invoked for the current transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID is written to the plain-text statement file as field ST-TRANID and to the HTML file as an HTML paragraph element; the Transaction Description is written to the plain-text statement file as field ST-TRANDT and to the HTML file as an HTML paragraph element; the Transaction Amount is written to the plain-text statement file as field ST-TRANAMT and to the HTML file as an HTML paragraph element; all three fields appear together as one transaction line in both output files

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Transaction Line to Plain Text and HTML Statement Files
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each retrieved transaction, the program invokes the transaction writing routine (6000-WRITE-TRANS) which outputs the transaction details — Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount — simultaneously to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML-formatted statement file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction line has been written to both output files, and the current transaction's amount is available in the active transaction amount field (TRNX-AMT), and a running statement total accumulator (WS-TOTAL-AMT) is maintained for the current customer statement
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction amount accumulation step is executed after writing the transaction line
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction's amount (TRNX-AMT) is added to the running statement total (WS-TOTAL-AMT), increasing the cumulative total by the exact amount of the current transaction; this updated total will continue to accumulate for all remaining transactions of the current card before being written as the final statement total

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accumulate Transaction Amount to Running Statement Total
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each transaction line is written, the transaction's monetary amount is added to the running total for the current customer statement. This running total accumulates across all transactions for the current card and is ultimately written as the statement's total transaction amount.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The scan of the in-memory transaction table is active, and the stored card number at the current index position (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) has been compared against the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The stored card number does not equal the XREF card number (no match found)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: No transactions are retrieved or written for the current card entry; the card index (CR-JMP) is incremented by 1 to advance to the next stored card entry; the scan termination conditions (all cards scanned OR stored card number exceeds XREF card number) are re-evaluated before any further processing

all_rules.Rule_Name: Skip Non-Matching Card Entry and Advance to Next Stored Card
all_rules.Rule_Description: When the stored card number at the current table index does not match the XREF card number, the current card entry is skipped entirely with no transaction processing, and the scan advances to the next card entry in the in-memory table. The scan termination conditions are then re-evaluated before examining the next entry.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A matching transaction record has been identified for the current customer's card number, containing a Transaction ID (TRNX-ID), a Transaction Description (TRNX-DESC), and a Transaction Amount (TRNX-AMT)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system prepares to write the transaction line to the output statement files
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID from the source transaction record is assigned to the statement Transaction ID output field (ST-TRANID); the Transaction Description from the source transaction record is assigned to the statement Transaction Description output field (ST-TRANDT); and the Transaction Amount from the source transaction record is assigned to the statement Transaction Amount output field (ST-TRANAMT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Populate Transaction Output Fields from Source Transaction Record
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before writing any transaction output, the system maps the three core transaction data elements — Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount — from the source transaction record into the statement output fields used for both plain text and HTML rendering.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The transaction output fields (Transaction ID, Transaction Description, Transaction Amount) have been populated from the source transaction record for the current transaction being processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the transaction detail to the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A single formatted transaction line (ST-LINE14) containing the Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount is written as one record to the plain text statement output file (STMT-FILE)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Formatted Transaction Line to Plain Text Statement File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each individual transaction is written as a single formatted line to the plain text statement file, combining the Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount together on one output line.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The plain text transaction line has been written to the statement file and the system is now preparing to write the same transaction to the HTML statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system begins writing the HTML representation of the current transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new HTML table row opening tag is written to the HTML file, followed by the opening HTML table data cell structure for the first column (Transaction ID column), establishing the HTML row container for the current transaction's data

all_rules.Rule_Name: Begin HTML Transaction Row Structure in HTML Statement File
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before writing any transaction data fields to the HTML statement file, the system opens a new HTML table row structure to contain the transaction's ID, description, and amount as separate HTML table data cells.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The HTML transaction row has been opened and the Transaction ID output field (ST-TRANID) has been populated with the current transaction's identifier
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the Transaction ID to the HTML statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then:
The Transaction ID value is wrapped in an HTML paragraph tag (formatted as '

' + Transaction ID value + '

') and written as a record to the HTML file; the HTML table data cell for the Transaction ID column is then closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Transaction ID as HTML Paragraph Element in HTML Statement File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction ID for each transaction is written to the HTML statement file as an HTML paragraph element enclosed within an HTML table data cell, ensuring the Transaction ID is properly formatted and displayed in the HTML statement output.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction ID has been written and its HTML table data cell has been closed; the Transaction Description output field (ST-TRANDT) has been populated with the current transaction's description
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the Transaction Description to the HTML statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then:
A new HTML table data cell column is opened for the description; the Transaction Description value is wrapped in an HTML paragraph tag (formatted as '

' + Transaction Description value + '

') and written as a record to the HTML file; the HTML table data cell for the Transaction Description column is then closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Transaction Description as HTML Paragraph Element in HTML Statement File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Description for each transaction is written to the HTML statement file as an HTML paragraph element enclosed within its own HTML table data cell, following the Transaction ID cell in the same HTML table row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction Description has been written and its HTML table data cell has been closed; the Transaction Amount output field (ST-TRANAMT) has been populated with the current transaction's monetary amount
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the Transaction Amount to the HTML statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then:
A new HTML table data cell column is opened for the amount; the Transaction Amount value is wrapped in an HTML paragraph tag (formatted as '

' + Transaction Amount value + '

') and written as a record to the HTML file; the HTML table data cell for the Transaction Amount column is then closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Transaction Amount as HTML Paragraph Element in HTML Statement File
all_rules.Rule_Description: The Transaction Amount for each transaction is written to the HTML statement file as an HTML paragraph element enclosed within its own HTML table data cell, following the Transaction Description cell in the same HTML table row.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All three transaction fields — Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount — have been written to the HTML file as HTML paragraph elements within their respective HTML table data cells for the current transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system finalizes the HTML representation of the current transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: An HTML table row closing tag is written to the HTML file, completing the HTML table row for the current transaction and ensuring the HTML output is properly structured for rendering

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close HTML Transaction Row After All Transaction Fields Are Written
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all three transaction data fields (Transaction ID, Transaction Description, Transaction Amount) have been written to the HTML file as individual HTML table data cells, the HTML table row for the current transaction must be explicitly closed to complete the well-formed HTML structure.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card number from the cross-reference record (XREF-CARD-NUM) has been matched to a card group entry (WS-CARD-NUM) in the in-memory transaction table, and the total number of transactions for that card group is stored in WS-TRCT for the current card index (CR-JMP)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction iterator (TR-JMP) is evaluated against the total transaction count (WS-TRCT) for the current card group
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If TR-JMP is less than or equal to WS-TRCT, there are more transactions to process and the next transaction is retrieved from the in-memory table; if TR-JMP exceeds WS-TRCT, all transactions for this card have been processed and the loop exits to compute the statement total

all_rules.Rule_Name: Determine If More Transactions Exist for Current Card
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each card number matched to the current XREF record, the program determines whether additional transactions remain to be processed by comparing the current transaction index against the total transaction count stored for that card group in the in-memory transaction table.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction record has been retrieved from the in-memory transaction table for the current card number, with Transaction ID (TRNX-ID), Transaction Description (TRNX-DESC), and Transaction Amount (TRNX-AMT) populated from the stored transaction data (WS-TRAN-NUM and WS-TRAN-REST)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The transaction detail writing step is executed for the current transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID is moved to the statement transaction ID field (ST-TRANID), the Transaction Description is moved to the statement transaction description field (ST-TRANDT), the Transaction Amount is moved to the statement transaction amount field (ST-TRANAMT), and one transaction detail line (ST-LINE14) is written to the plain-text statement file (FD-STMTFILE-REC); additionally, the Transaction ID, Description, and Amount are each written as separate HTML paragraph elements to the HTML statement file (FD-HTMLFILE-REC)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Individual Transaction Detail Line to Statement and HTML Output
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction belonging to the current card number, the transaction details — Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount — are written as a single line to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML-formatted statement file.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction detail line has been written for the current transaction, the Transaction Amount (TRNX-AMT) is available from the in-memory transaction table entry (WS-TRAN-REST), and the running account total (WS-TOTAL-AMT) has been initialized to zero at the start of the current customer-account statement cycle
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The accumulation step is executed after writing the transaction detail line
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction Amount (TRNX-AMT) is added to the running account total (WS-TOTAL-AMT), resulting in WS-TOTAL-AMT reflecting the cumulative sum of all transaction amounts processed so far for the current card number on the current account statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accumulate Running Total of Transaction Amounts for Current Account Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each transaction detail line is written, the transaction amount is added to the running total for the current account statement. This running total accumulates the total expenditure across all transactions associated with the current card number and is reset to zero at the start of each new customer-account statement cycle.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transactions for the current card number have been processed, and the running account total (WS-TOTAL-AMT) contains the complete sum of all transaction amounts for the current account statement
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The total transfer step is executed after the transaction processing loop exits
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The accumulated total (WS-TOTAL-AMT) is moved to the intermediate total field (WS-TRN-AMT), and WS-TRN-AMT is then moved to the statement total amount output field (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT), making the total expenditure available for writing to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML statement file as the statement summary total line

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Accumulated Total to Statement Output Field for Display
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all transactions for the current card number have been processed and their amounts accumulated, the final running total is transferred to the statement output field so it can be displayed as the total expenditure on both the plain-text and HTML statement outputs.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transactions for the current account-card combination have been written to the statement, and the running total amount (WS-TOTAL-AMT) holds the sum of all transaction amounts processed for this account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The statement total and footer writing process is triggered after the last transaction for the account is written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The running total amount (WS-TOTAL-AMT) must be moved to the intermediate total amount field (WS-TRN-AMT), and then WS-TRN-AMT must be moved to the statement total amount field (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT), so that the formatted total is available for writing to the plain text statement file

all_rules.Rule_Name: Transfer Running Total to Statement Total Amount Field
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all transactions for an account have been written, the accumulated running total transaction amount is transferred through an intermediate working storage field into the statement total amount field, making it ready for formatted output on the plain text statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The statement total amount field (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT) has been populated with the formatted total transaction amount for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The statement total and footer writing process writes the separator line
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Statement separator line (ST-LINE12) must be written to the plain text statement file (FD-STMTFILE-REC) as the first output line in the statement footer section

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Separator Line to Plain Text Statement File
all_rules.Rule_Description: A visual separator line is written to the plain text statement file to delineate the transaction section from the total expenditure amount line, providing clear formatting and readability in the output statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The separator line has been written to the plain text statement file, and the statement total amount field (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT) contains the formatted sum of all transaction amounts for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The total expenditure amount line is written to the plain text statement file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total expenditure amount line (ST-LINE14A), which contains the formatted total transaction amount (ST-TOTAL-TRAMT), must be written to the plain text statement file (FD-STMTFILE-REC) immediately after the separator line

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Total Expenditure Amount Line to Plain Text Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: The formatted total expenditure amount, representing the sum of all transaction amounts for the current account, is written to the plain text statement file as a labeled summary line, giving the customer a clear view of their total spending.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The total expenditure amount line has been written to the plain text statement file for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-statement banner is written as the final footer element
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The end-of-statement banner line (ST-LINE15) must be written to the plain text statement file (FD-STMTFILE-REC) as the last line of the current account statement, completing the plain text statement for that account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write End-of-Statement Banner to Plain Text Statement File
all_rules.Rule_Description: An end-of-statement banner line is written to the plain text statement file as the final line of the current customer account statement, clearly marking the conclusion of the statement for the account before the next customer's statement begins.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All transaction detail rows for the current account have been written to the HTML statement file, and the total transaction amount summary has been written
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The HTML statement footer section is being written for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: A new HTML table row opening tag (HTML-LTRS) is written to the HTML statement file (FD-HTMLFILE-REC) to begin the footer row structure

all_rules.Rule_Name: Open New HTML Table Row for Statement Footer
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all transactions for an account have been written to the HTML statement file, a new HTML table row is opened to contain the End of Statement marker, ensuring the footer content is properly structured within the HTML table.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A new HTML table row has been opened in the HTML statement file for the current account's footer section
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The End of Statement marker is being written to the HTML file
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The HTML line HTML-L75, representing the 'End of Statement' content, is written to the HTML statement file (FD-HTMLFILE-REC) as a fixed HTML line, signaling the conclusion of transaction data for the current account

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write End of Statement Marker to HTML File
all_rules.Rule_Description: After opening the footer table row, the 'End of Statement' content marker (HTML-L75) is written to the HTML statement file to clearly indicate to the reader that no further transactions exist for the current account statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The End of Statement marker (HTML-L75) has been written to the HTML statement file for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The HTML table data cell and table row closing tags are being written
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: First, the HTML table data cell closing tag (HTML-LTDE) is written to the HTML statement file (FD-HTMLFILE-REC), followed immediately by the HTML table row closing tag (HTML-LTRE) written to the HTML statement file (FD-HTMLFILE-REC), ensuring both the cell and row are properly closed in sequence

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close HTML Table Data Cell and Table Row for Statement Footer
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the End of Statement marker is written, the HTML table data cell and the HTML table row must be properly closed to maintain valid HTML structure for the account statement document.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The HTML table data cell and table row closing tags have been written for the current account's footer section
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The HTML table closing tag is being written to finalize the table structure
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The HTML table closing tag (HTML-L78) is written to the HTML statement file (FD-HTMLFILE-REC) as a fixed HTML line, completing the HTML table structure for the current account statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Closing HTML Table Tag to Complete Table Structure
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the footer row is closed, the entire HTML table structure that contains the account statement — including the header, customer details, and all transaction rows — must be formally closed with a closing table tag to produce a valid HTML document.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The HTML table closing tag (HTML-L78) has been written to the HTML statement file for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The HTML body closing tag is being written to finalize the body section
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The HTML body closing tag (HTML-L79) is written to the HTML statement file (FD-HTMLFILE-REC) as a fixed HTML line, completing the HTML body section for the current account statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Closing HTML Body Tag to Complete Body Section
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the HTML table is closed, the HTML body section that contains all visible account statement content must be formally closed to produce a structurally valid HTML document for the current account.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The HTML body closing tag (HTML-L79) has been written to the HTML statement file for the current account, and all statement content including customer details, transactions, total amount, and End of Statement marker have been written
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The final closing HTML document tag is being written to complete the HTML statement
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The HTML document closing tag (HTML-L80) is written to the HTML statement file (FD-HTMLFILE-REC) as a fixed HTML line, completing and finalizing the entire HTML account statement document for the current account, after which the HTML statement for this account is fully complete

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Closing HTML Document Tag to Complete HTML Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: As the final step in producing the HTML account statement for the current account, the closing HTML document tag must be written to formally complete and seal the HTML file, making it a fully valid and renderable HTML document.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A statement header has been successfully written for the current customer account, containing the customer full name, address, account ID, current balance, and FICO credit score, and the system is about to begin retrieving and accumulating transaction amounts for that account
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system transitions from writing the account statement header to processing the transactions for the current account
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The total transaction amount accumulator (WS-TOTAL-AMT) must be set to zero before any transaction amounts are retrieved or added, ensuring the running total starts fresh for each account and does not include any transaction amounts from previously processed accounts

all_rules.Rule_Name: Reset Total Transaction Amount Before Processing Each Account Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Before retrieving and accumulating transaction amounts for a new account statement, the running total transaction amount accumulator must be reset to zero. This ensures that the total amount displayed on each account statement reflects only the transactions belonging to that specific account, and not carried-over amounts from previously processed accounts.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All cross-reference records have been fully processed and the main processing loop has ended
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the file management service (CBSTM03B) with a Close operation request for the Transaction File (TRNXFILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction File (TRNXFILE) is successfully closed; if the close operation does not complete successfully, the program terminates abnormally with an error message indicating 'ERROR CLOSING TRNXFILE'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Transaction File After Processing Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once all cross-reference records have been processed, the Transaction File (TRNXFILE) must be formally closed through the file management service to release all associated resources and finalize any pending operations.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction File (TRNXFILE) has been successfully closed and all cross-reference records have been processed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the file management service (CBSTM03B) with a Close operation request for the Cross-Reference File (XREFFILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Cross-Reference File (XREFFILE) is successfully closed; if the close operation does not complete successfully, the program terminates abnormally with an error message indicating 'ERROR CLOSING XREFFILE'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Cross-Reference File After Processing Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Transaction File has been closed, the Cross-Reference File (XREFFILE) must be formally closed through the file management service to release all associated resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Cross-Reference File (XREFFILE) has been successfully closed and all customer data lookups have been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the file management service (CBSTM03B) with a Close operation request for the Customer Master File (CUSTFILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Customer Master File (CUSTFILE) is successfully closed; if the close operation does not complete successfully, the program terminates abnormally with an error message indicating 'ERROR CLOSING CUSTFILE'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Customer Master File After Processing Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Cross-Reference File has been closed, the Customer Master File (CUSTFILE) must be formally closed through the file management service to release all associated resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Customer Master File (CUSTFILE) has been successfully closed and all account data lookups have been completed
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system invokes the file management service (CBSTM03B) with a Close operation request for the Account Master File (ACCTFILE)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Account Master File (ACCTFILE) is successfully closed; if the close operation does not complete successfully, the program terminates abnormally with an error message indicating 'ERROR CLOSING ACCTFILE'

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Account Master File After Processing Completion
all_rules.Rule_Description: After the Customer Master File has been closed, the Account Master File (ACCTFILE) must be formally closed through the file management service to release all associated resources.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: All four input files (TRNXFILE, XREFFILE, CUSTFILE, ACCTFILE) have been successfully closed and all customer account statements have been written
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system closes both the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE) and the HTML statement file (HTML-FILE) in a single close operation
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Both the plain text statement file (STMT-FILE) and the HTML statement file (HTML-FILE) are successfully closed, ensuring all generated statement content is permanently saved and available for downstream use

all_rules.Rule_Name: Close Plain Text and HTML Statement Output Files
all_rules.Rule_Description: After all input files have been closed, both the plain text statement output file (STMT-FILE) and the HTML statement output file (HTML-FILE) must be closed together to finalize and flush all written statement content to permanent storage.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The main processing loop has completed, meaning all cross-reference records have been read and all corresponding customer statements have been generated and written
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The end-of-file condition is reached on the Cross-Reference File and the program exits the main processing loop
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: Files are closed in the following mandatory sequence: (1) Transaction File (TRNXFILE), (2) Cross-Reference File (XREFFILE), (3) Customer Master File (CUSTFILE), (4) Account Master File (ACCTFILE), (5) Plain Text Statement File (STMT-FILE) and HTML Statement File (HTML-FILE) together — no file closure may be skipped or reordered, and the program terminates normally only after all six files are closed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Enforce Sequential File Closure Order After All Records Processed
all_rules.Rule_Description: All six files used during statement generation must be closed in a strict, mandatory sequence after the main processing loop completes. The closure order ensures data integrity: input files are closed before output files, and the transaction file is closed first as it was opened and fully loaded first.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The in-memory transaction table has been pre-loaded with card entries and their associated transactions, and a current XREF card number is available for matching
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program begins the process of finding transactions for the current XREF card number
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card table scan index (CR-JMP) is initialized to 1, starting the search from the first stored card entry in the in-memory transaction table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Initialize Card Table Scan from First Entry
all_rules.Rule_Description: When matching transactions to a customer's XREF card number, the scan of the in-memory transaction table always begins at the very first stored card entry, ensuring no transactions are missed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card table scan is in progress and the scan index (CR-JMP) is being incremented through the stored card entries
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The scan index (CR-JMP) exceeds the total count of stored card entries (CR-CNT), meaning every stored card entry has been visited
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card table scan terminates immediately and no further card entries are examined

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Card Table Scan When All Entries Exhausted
all_rules.Rule_Description: The scan of the in-memory transaction table stops when all stored card entries have been examined, preventing any out-of-bounds access to the table.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card table scan is in progress and the in-memory transaction table entries are ordered by card number
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The stored card number at the current scan position (WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP) is greater than the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM) being matched
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card table scan terminates immediately, as no matching card number can exist at any subsequent position in the ordered table

all_rules.Rule_Name: Stop Card Table Scan When Stored Card Number Exceeds XREF Card Number
all_rules.Rule_Description: Because the in-memory transaction table is ordered by card number, the scan stops early as soon as the current stored card number is greater than the XREF card number being searched, since no match can exist beyond that point.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The card table scan is active and the current scan position points to a stored card entry with card number WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP, and the XREF record provides the target card number XREF-CARD-NUM
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The stored card number (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is evaluated against the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: If the stored card number exactly equals the XREF card number, the card is identified as a match and its transactions are eligible for statement inclusion; if the stored card number does not equal the XREF card number, the entry is skipped and the scan advances to the next stored card entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Identify Matching Card Number in Transaction Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: During the card table scan, each stored card number is compared against the current XREF card number to determine whether transactions for that card should be included in the customer's statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A stored card number (WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP) has been confirmed to exactly match the XREF card number (XREF-CARD-NUM)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The match is confirmed and transaction processing is about to begin for this card
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The matched card number (WS-CARD-NUM at CR-JMP) is copied into the transaction card number field (TRNX-CARD-NUM), establishing it as the active card number for all subsequent transaction retrieval and output operations for this statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Matched Card Number for Transaction Retrieval
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a stored card number matches the XREF card number, the matched card number is recorded as the active card number to be used during the retrieval and writing of all associated transactions.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card entry in the in-memory transaction table has been matched to the XREF card number, and the matched card entry contains a count of transactions (WS-TRCT at CR-JMP) with each transaction storing a Transaction ID (WS-TRAN-NUM) and transaction details including description and amount (WS-TRAN-REST)
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The program iterates through all transactions for the matched card, from the first transaction up to and including the last transaction as defined by the stored transaction count (WS-TRCT at CR-JMP)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: For each transaction: the Transaction ID (WS-TRAN-NUM at CR-JMP, TR-JMP) is set as the current transaction identifier (TRNX-ID), the transaction details (WS-TRAN-REST at CR-JMP, TR-JMP) including description and amount are set as the current transaction data (TRNX-REST), the transaction is written to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML statement file, and the transaction amount (TRNX-AMT) is added to the running statement total (WS-TOTAL-AMT)

all_rules.Rule_Name: Process All Transactions for a Matched Card
all_rules.Rule_Description: Once a card number match is found, every transaction stored under that card in the in-memory table is retrieved and written to the customer statement, and each transaction amount is added to the running statement total.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The current stored card entry at scan index CR-JMP has been fully evaluated, either resulting in a match with transactions processed or a non-match that was skipped
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The evaluation of the current card entry is complete and the stop conditions (all entries scanned OR stored card number exceeds XREF card number) have not yet been met
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The card table scan index (CR-JMP) is incremented by 1 to point to the next stored card entry, and the stop conditions are re-evaluated before examining the next entry

all_rules.Rule_Name: Advance to Next Card Table Entry After Evaluation
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each stored card entry has been evaluated — whether it matched the XREF card number or not — the scan index advances by one to move to the next stored card entry, ensuring every card entry is considered until a stop condition is met.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card number match has been found between the XREF card number and a card number stored in the in-memory transaction table at position CR-JMP
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system confirms the card numbers are equal (XREF-CARD-NUM = WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The matched card number from the in-memory table (WS-CARD-NUM at index CR-JMP) is assigned as the current transaction card number (TRNX-CARD-NUM) to identify all transactions belonging to this card for the current statement

all_rules.Rule_Name: Set Current Card Number for Transaction Processing
all_rules.Rule_Description: When a card number match is found between the cross-reference file and the in-memory transaction table, the matched card number is set as the current card number to be used for all subsequent transaction processing for that statement.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A card number match has been confirmed and the current card group at index CR-JMP has a total transaction count stored as WS-TRCT at index CR-JMP
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system iterates through transactions using a counter TR-JMP starting at 1 and incrementing by 1 for each transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The iteration continues processing each transaction as long as TR-JMP does not exceed the total transaction count (WS-TRCT at index CR-JMP); when TR-JMP exceeds WS-TRCT, all transactions for this card have been processed and the loop terminates

all_rules.Rule_Name: Iterate Through All Transactions for Matched Card
all_rules.Rule_Description: After a card number match is found, the system iterates through every transaction stored in the in-memory table for that card, processing each one individually until all transactions for the matched card have been processed.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The system is iterating through transactions for a matched card at card index CR-JMP and current transaction index TR-JMP within the in-memory transaction table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system accesses the in-memory transaction table at the two-dimensional position identified by card index CR-JMP and transaction index TR-JMP
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID stored at WS-TRAN-NUM (CR-JMP, TR-JMP) in the in-memory table is retrieved and set as the current Transaction ID (TRNX-ID) for use in statement output

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Transaction ID from In-Memory Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction belonging to the matched card, the unique Transaction ID is retrieved from the in-memory transaction table using the current card index and transaction index as lookup coordinates.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction ID has been retrieved for the current transaction at card index CR-JMP and transaction index TR-JMP in the in-memory transaction table
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system accesses the remaining transaction data stored at WS-TRAN-REST at the two-dimensional position (CR-JMP, TR-JMP) in the in-memory table
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The full transaction details (TRNX-REST — containing transaction description, amount, date, and all other transaction attributes) are retrieved and made available for statement writing, including TRNX-AMT, TRNX-DESC, and all other transaction fields

all_rules.Rule_Name: Retrieve Transaction Details from In-Memory Table
all_rules.Rule_Description: For each transaction belonging to the matched card, the full transaction details (including transaction description, amount, date, and other attributes) are retrieved from the in-memory transaction table using the current card index and transaction index.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: The Transaction ID (TRNX-ID), Transaction Description (TRNX-DESC), and Transaction Amount (TRNX-AMT) have been retrieved from the in-memory table for the current transaction
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system writes the transaction details to both output files by invoking the transaction writing routine (6000-WRITE-TRANS)
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The Transaction ID is written to the plain-text statement line (ST-TRANID) and as an HTML paragraph in the HTML file; the Transaction Description is written to the plain-text statement (ST-TRANDT) and as an HTML paragraph; the Transaction Amount is written to the plain-text statement (ST-TRANAMT) and as an HTML paragraph — all formatted as a single transaction row in both output files

all_rules.Rule_Name: Write Transaction Line to Plain Text and HTML Statement
all_rules.Rule_Description: Each individual transaction is written simultaneously to both the plain-text statement file and the HTML statement file. The transaction line includes the Transaction ID, Transaction Description, and Transaction Amount formatted appropriately for each output format.

Acceptance_Criteria.Given: A transaction has been successfully written to both the plain-text and HTML statement files, and the current transaction amount (TRNX-AMT) is available from the retrieved transaction details
Acceptance_Criteria.When: The system processes each transaction within the matched card's transaction list
Acceptance_Criteria.Then: The current transaction amount (TRNX-AMT) is added to the cumulative running total (WS-TOTAL-AMT), which accumulates the sum of all transaction amounts for the current card; this total is reset to zero at the start of each new customer statement cycle and will be written as the statement total after all transactions are processed

all_rules.Rule_Name: Accumulate Transaction Amount to Running Total
all_rules.Rule_Description: After each transaction is written to the statement, the transaction amount is added to a running total that will represent the total transaction amount for the current customer account statement.

description:
CBSTM03A is a batch COBOL program in the CardDemo application that generates credit card account statements from transaction data. It reads transaction, cross-reference, customer, and account files via a called subroutine (CBSTM03B), then produces account statements in two formats: plain text and HTML, each containing customer details, account information, FICO score, and a transaction summary with totals. This is a Main/Driver program as it drives the overall processing flow, opens and closes all files, and calls CBSTM03B as a subordinate module.
- **Execution Environment**: Batch - **Database Access**: FILE (Sequential/VSAM via subroutine CBSTM03B) - **MQ Calls**: No - **Module Type**: Main/Driver module
### Key Functionalities: 1: Initialize Output Files - Open plain text statement file (STMT-FILE) and HTML file (HTML-FILE) for output, and initialize the transaction table and counter structures before processing begins 2: Load Transaction File into Memory Table - Read all records from the transaction file sequentially and load them into a two-dimensional in-memory table organized by card number, storing up to 51 card numbers each with up to 10 transactions, tracking transaction counts per card 3: Group Transactions by Card Number - While loading transactions, detect card number changes to group transactions under their respective card numbers, maintaining a count of transactions per card and a count of unique cards 4: Open Cross-Reference File - Open the card-to-customer/account cross-reference file (XREFFILE) to enable lookup of customer and account information for each card number 5: Open Customer File - Open the customer master file (CUSTFILE) to enable retrieval of customer demographic and address information by customer ID 6: Open Account File - Open the account master file (ACCTFILE) to enable retrieval of account balance and credit score information by account ID 7: Read Next Cross-Reference Record - Sequentially read the next record from the cross-reference file to obtain the card number, associated customer ID, and account ID for statement generation; set end-of-file flag when all records are processed 8: Retrieve Customer Information - Using the customer ID from the cross-reference record, perform a key-based lookup in the customer file to retrieve the customer's full name, address lines, state, country, zip code, and FICO credit score 9: Retrieve Account Information - Using the account ID from the cross-reference record, perform a key-based lookup in the account file to retrieve the account ID and current balance 10: Format Customer Name - Concatenate customer first name, middle name, and last name into a single formatted name string for display on the statement 11: Format Customer Address - Populate address line 1, address line 2, and combine address line 3 with state code, country code, and zip code into a formatted address string for the statement 12: Write Plain Text Statement Header - Write the start-of-statement banner, customer name, address lines, separator lines, Basic Details section heading, account ID, current balance, and FICO score to the plain text statement file 13: Write HTML Document Header - Write the HTML document structure tags (DOCTYPE, html, head, meta, title, body, table) and the statement account number heading to the HTML output file 14: Write HTML Bank Identification Section - Write the bank name (Bank of XYZ), address (410 Terry Ave N, Seattle WA 99999) as the issuing bank information in the HTML statement 15: Write HTML Customer Name and Address - Write the customer full name and all address lines as HTML paragraph elements in the HTML statement file 16: Write HTML Basic Details Section - Write the account ID, current balance, and FICO credit score as HTML formatted content under the Basic Details section heading in the HTML statement 17: Write HTML Transaction Summary Header - Write the Transaction Summary section heading and column headers (Tran ID, Tran Details, Amount) as HTML table rows in the HTML statement file 18: Write Plain Text Transaction Summary Column Headers - Write the transaction summary section heading, separator lines, and column headers (Tran ID, Tran Details, Tran Amount) to the plain text statement file 19: Match and Retrieve Transactions for Card - Search the in-memory transaction table for entries matching the current card number from the cross-reference record, iterating through all stored transactions for that card 20: Write Individual Transaction Line - For each matching transaction, write the transaction ID, transaction description, and transaction amount as a formatted line to both the plain text statement file and as an HTML table row in the HTML file 21: Accumulate Total Transaction Amount - Add each transaction amount to a running total for the current account statement to compute the total expenditure 22: Write Statement Total and Footer - After all transactions for the account are written, format and write the total expenditure amount and the end-of-statement banner to the plain text statement file 23: Write HTML Statement Footer - Write the End of Statement marker and closing HTML tags (table, body, html) to complete the HTML statement file for the current account 24: Reset Statement Totals - Reset the total transaction amount accumulator to zero before processing the next account's statement 25: Close All Input and Output Files - After all cross-reference records are processed, close the transaction file, cross-reference file, customer file, account file, plain text statement file, and HTML statement file
